meta.title: Disease Management Library

schema.pharmacological: Array ordered by line of therapy (first-line first, then second-line, etc.)

meta.disclaimer: Educational reference compiled from major international guidelines (ESC, AHA/ACC, GOLD, GINA, KDIGO, ADA, NICE, IDSA, ESMO, NCCN, EULAR, WHO, CDC, and others) current up to 2025. Drug names, doses, and line ordering vary by country and change over time. ALWAYS verify against your local formulary and current guidelines before clinical use. Not a substitute for clinical judgment.

non_pharmacological: DASH diet rich in fruits/vegetables and low-fat dairy
Sodium restriction to <2 g/day (5 g salt)
Weight loss (target BMI <25; ~1 mmHg SBP per kg lost)
Regular aerobic exercise 150 min/week plus resistance training
Limit alcohol (<=2 drinks/day men, <=1 women)
Smoking cessation
Screen and treat obstructive sleep apnea
Increase dietary potassium (unless CKD/hyperkalemia)

pharmacological.regimen: Dual low-dose combination: ACE inhibitor or ARB + CCB (amlodipine) or thiazide-like diuretic (chlorthalidone or indapamide) as single-pill combo; monotherapy acceptable in low-risk grade 1 HTN or age >80/frail
Triple combination: ACEi/ARB + CCB + thiazide-like diuretic at full doses
Add spironolactone 25-50 mg if K+ <=4.5; alternatives amiloride, doxazosin, eplerenone, or bisoprolol
Expert referral; exclude secondary causes; consider renal denervation in selected patients

non_pharmacological: Screen in young onset (<40 grade 2), resistant HTN, or abrupt onset: renal artery stenosis, primary aldosteronism, pheochromocytoma, Cushing, thyroid disease, coarctation, OSA, drugs (NSAIDs, OCP, steroids, stimulants)

pharmacological.regimen: Primary aldosteronism: spironolactone/eplerenone or adrenalectomy if unilateral adenoma; renovascular: revascularization for selected cases; pheochromocytoma: alpha-blockade (phenoxybenzamine/doxazosin) BEFORE beta-blockade, then surgery

non_pharmacological: Admit to ICU/HDU with continuous BP monitoring
Identify target-organ damage (encephalopathy, ACS, pulmonary edema, dissection, eclampsia, AKI)

pharmacological.regimen: IV titratable agent: labetalol or nicardipine/clevidipine; reduce MAP ~20-25% in first hour then gradually, EXCEPT aortic dissection (SBP <120 in 20 min) and acute ischemic stroke (permissive unless thrombolysis)
Pulmonary edema: IV nitroglycerin + loop diuretic; ACS: nitroglycerin + beta-blocker; eclampsia: MgSO4 + labetalol/hydralazine; catecholamine crisis: IV phentolamine
Overlap with oral agents and wean IV over 24-48 h

non_pharmacological: Smoking cessation
Cardiac rehabilitation and regular exercise
Mediterranean diet, weight control
Treat comorbidities (HTN, diabetes, OSA, anemia)
Influenza vaccination

pharmacological.regimen: High-intensity statin (atorvastatin 40-80 mg) +/- ezetimibe to LDL targets; aspirin 75-100 mg (clopidogrel if intolerant); ACEi/ARB especially if LVEF <40%, DM, CKD or HTN
Beta-blocker and/or non-dihydropyridine CCB (verapamil/diltiazem)
Add long-acting nitrate, ivabradine, ranolazine, nicorandil or trimetazidine
PCI or CABG for limiting symptoms despite OMT or high-risk anatomy (e.g., left main / multivessel with reduced EF favor CABG)

non_pharmacological: Immediate ECG within 10 min, activate cath lab
Primary PCI is preferred reperfusion (FMC-to-wire <90 min at PCI center; <120 min if transferred)
Cardiac rehabilitation after stabilization

pharmacological.regimen: Primary PCI; if not achievable within 120 min give fibrinolytic (tenecteplase/alteplase) within 10 min then transfer (pharmaco-invasive PCI 2-24 h)
Aspirin 150-300 mg + P2Y12 inhibitor (prasugrel or ticagrelor preferred; clopidogrel with fibrinolysis or high bleeding risk) + parenteral anticoagulation (UFH, bivalirudin or enoxaparin)
High-intensity statin +/- ezetimibe/PCSK9i; beta-blocker; ACEi/ARB (especially EF <40%, DM, CKD, HTN); eplerenone if EF <=40% with HF or diabetes; DAPT 12 months (shorter if high bleeding risk)
Cardiogenic shock: norepinephrine +/- inotrope, urgent revascularization; ICD if EF <=35% persists >=40 days post-MI despite OMT

non_pharmacological: Risk stratify with GRACE score; continuous monitoring
Immediate invasive (<2 h) if very high risk (shock, refractory pain, life-threatening arrhythmia); early invasive (<24 h) if high risk (GRACE >140, dynamic ST changes, troponin rise/fall)

pharmacological.regimen: Aspirin + P2Y12 inhibitor (ticagrelor or prasugrel after anatomy defined; clopidogrel alternative) + anticoagulation (fondaparinux, enoxaparin or UFH)
Beta-blocker, nitrates for pain, high-intensity statin, ACEi/ARB
DAPT 12 months (de-escalation or shorter duration considered if high bleeding risk); add low-dose rivaroxaban 2.5 mg BID (COMPASS-style) in select high ischemic risk

non_pharmacological: Smoking cessation (most important)
Avoid cold exposure, cocaine/amphetamines, hyperventilation triggers

pharmacological.regimen: Calcium channel blocker (diltiazem, amlodipine or nifedipine) at adequate dose
Add long-acting nitrate
Non-selective beta-blockers and triptans can worsen spasm

diseases.disease: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)
non_pharmacological: Sodium moderation and fluid restriction in hyponatremic/severe HF
Daily weight monitoring; diuretic self-titration plan
Cardiac rehabilitation and regular aerobic exercise
Influenza, pneumococcal and SARS-CoV-2 vaccination
Avoid NSAIDs, non-dihydropyridine CCBs, most antiarrhythmics, TZDs
Treat iron deficiency (IV iron), anemia, OSA; alcohol abstinence if alcoholic CMP
ICD/CRT evaluation per criteria

pharmacological.regimen: 1) ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan; ACEi if ARNI unavailable - switch ACEi to ARNI with 36 h washout) 2) Evidence-based beta-blocker (bisoprolol, carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, nebivolol) 3) MRA (spironolactone or eplerenone) 4) SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin)
Loop diuretics (furosemide/torsemide) titrated to euvolemia

Hydralazine + isosorbide dinitrate (self-identified African ancestry or ACEi/ARB/ARNI intolerance); ivabradine if sinus rhythm HR >=70 on max beta-blocker; vericiguat after recent worsening HF; digoxin for symptoms or rate control in AF
ICD (primary prevention if EF <=35% after >=3 months OMT); CRT if LBBB/QRS >=130-150 ms

diseases.disease: Heart failure with mildly reduced/preserved EF (HFmrEF/HFpEF)
non_pharmacological: Weight loss in obesity (including structured programs)
Regular exercise/cardiac rehab
Control BP, AF, diabetes, CKD, OSA
Sodium moderation, diuretics for congestion

pharmacological.regimen: SGLT2 inhibitor (empagliflozin EMPEROR-Preserved / dapagliflozin DELIVER) - class 1/2a recommendation for HFpEF and HFmrEF

Diuretics for congestion; optimize BP to <130/80; consider finerenone (FINEARTS-HF benefit), sacubitril/valsartan especially in lower-range EF (PARAGON-HF subgroup), MRAs and ARBs in selected patients
Semaglutide in obese HFpEF (STEP-HFpEF); treat AF (rate/rhythm, ablation), valvular disease, renal artery stenosis as indicated

non_pharmacological: Oxygen only if SpO2 <90%; non-invasive ventilation for pulmonary edema with respiratory distress
Daily weights, strict fluid balance; identify and treat precipitant (ACS, arrhythmia, infection, PE, non-adherence, thyroid)

pharmacological.regimen: IV loop diuretic (furosemide 20-40 mg or >= home oral dose IV); assess response at 2-6 h and double/escalate
Diuretic resistance: add thiazide-type (oral metolazone or IV chlorothiazide) or acetazolamide (ADVOR); IV vasodilators (nitroglycerin) if SBP adequate, especially hypertensive pulmonary edema
Inotropes (dobutamine or milrinone), norepinephrine for hypotension; consider mechanical circulatory support
Ultrafiltration; advanced HF referral (transplant/LVAD evaluation)

non_pharmacological: ICU care, arterial line, consider pulmonary artery catheter
Urgent echocardiography to exclude mechanical complications (rupture, acute MR/VSD)
Early revascularization for ACS cause

pharmacological.regimen: Norepinephrine (preferred over dopamine); add dobutamine or milrinone for low output
Vasopressin for refractory vasoplegia; avoid routine IABP (IABP-SHOCK II); consider Impella/VA-ECMO in selected centers
Correct acidosis, hypocalcemia; cautious fluids only if RV failure/volume responsive; mechanical support bridge to decision

non_pharmacological: Risk-factor management: weight loss, exercise, alcohol reduction, treat OSA and HTN (ABC pathway: Anticoagulation, Better symptom control, Cardiovascular risk)
Cardioversion (electrical or pharmacological) for new-onset or unstable AF

pharmacological.regimen: DOAC (apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, dabigatran) for CHA2DS2-VA score >=2 men / >=3 women (2024 ESC; consider at score 1 men / 2 women); warfarin (INR 2-3) only for mechanical valves or moderate-severe mitral stenosis
Beta-blocker or non-dihydropyridine CCB; digoxin in sedentary patients or HFrEF; amiodarone acutely in decompensated HF; lenient target resting HR <110 acceptable

Antiarrhythmics guided by structural heart disease: flecainide/propafenone (no structural disease; pill-in-pocket option), dronedarone or sotalol (caution), amiodarone if HFrEF; early rhythm control favored (EAST-AFNET 4)
Class I for selected symptomatic paroxysmal AF; first-line option in selected patients and in AF with HFrEF (CASTLE-AF)
Percutaneous LAAO if long-term anticoagulation contraindicated

non_pharmacological: Anticoagulation per AF risk score
Electrical cardioversion if unstable or early rhythm strategy

pharmacological.regimen: Beta-blocker or non-dihydropyridine CCB (often difficult to rate-control)
Cavotricuspid isthmus ablation for typical flutter (>90-95% cure, low risk) - preferred over long-term drugs
Ibutilide or high-rate pacing; avoid class Ic agents without AV-nodal blockade (1:1 conduction risk)

non_pharmacological: Vagal maneuvers first (modified Valsalva - REVERT technique)
Synchronized cardioversion if hemodynamically unstable

pharmacological.regimen: IV adenosine (6 mg, then 12 mg rapid bolus)
IV beta-blocker or verapamil/diltiazem
Catheter ablation first-line (curative, >95% success for slow-pathway modification); beta-blocker, verapamil or flecainide if ablation declined

non_pharmacological: Avoid AV-nodal blockers in pre-excited AF (verapamil, digoxin, IV beta-blockers, adenosine) - can accelerate conduction

pharmacological.regimen: Procainamide IV (or ibutilide) for stable pre-excited AF; immediate electrical cardioversion if unstable
Catheter ablation of accessory pathway (recommended for symptomatic patients and high-risk occupations)

non_pharmacological: Reassurance if structurally normal heart
Reduce caffeine, alcohol, stimulants; correct electrolytes; evaluate for PVC-induced cardiomyopathy if burden >10-15%

pharmacological.regimen: Beta-blocker or non-dihydropyridine CCB
Catheter ablation for high burden, symptomatic patients or PVC-induced cardiomyopathy; class Ic/III agents in selected cases

non_pharmacological: Immediate synchronized cardioversion if unstable
Identify and treat ischemia, electrolyte abnormalities, drugs

pharmacological.regimen: IV amiodarone, procainamide or sotalol; correct K+/Mg2+
ICD for survivors of VT/VF without reversible cause; beta-blocker in all; optimize HF therapy
Amiodarone + beta-blocker; catheter ablation (especially scar-related); sedation/autonomic modulation for electrical storm

diseases.disease: Torsades de pointes / long QT syndrome
non_pharmacological: Stop all QT-prolonging drugs; correct hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, bradycardia
Avoid QT drugs in congenital LQTS (crediblemeds.org list)

pharmacological.regimen: IV magnesium sulfate 2 g regardless of Mg level; overdrive pacing or isoproterenol for pause-dependent TdP (NOT in congenital LQTS)
Beta-blocker (nadolol/propranolol preferred) first-line; mexiletine in LQT3; left cardiac sympathetic denervation or ICD in high-risk/breakthrough events

non_pharmacological: Avoid fever (aggressive antipyresis), excess alcohol, and sodium-channel blockers
Genetic counseling; family screening

pharmacological.regimen: ICD for survivors of aborted SCD or sustained arrhythmias; quinidine for electrical storms or if ICD contraindicated; ablation of RVOT epicardial substrate in selected

non_pharmacological: Review and stop rate-slowing drugs; treat hypothyroidism, ischemia

pharmacological.regimen: Atropine 0.5-1 mg IV; transcutaneous pacing, dopamine or isoproterenol infusion if refractory
Permanent pacemaker for symptomatic bradycardia/pauses; dual-chamber preferred to reduce AF and pacemaker syndrome

non_pharmacological: Continuous monitoring; transcutaneous pacing pads ready; treat reversible causes (inferior MI, drugs, Lyme disease, hyperkalemia)

pharmacological.regimen: Atropine (works mainly for nodal block; unreliable in infranodal); isoproterenol or temporary transvenous pacing if unstable
Permanent pacemaker (CRT or His-bundle/left bundle area pacing if high ventricular pacing burden with reduced EF)

non_pharmacological: Alcohol abstinence if alcoholic CMP; avoid intense competitive sport during active disease
Genetic testing and family screening when idiopathic
Treat peripartum, tachycardia-mediated (ablate/rate control), and inflammatory causes

pharmacological.regimen: Full HFrEF four-pillar therapy (ARNI, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2i)
ICD for primary prevention if EF <=35% after >=3 months OMT (especially ischemic; shared decision in non-ischemic); CRT if wide LBBB
Immunosuppression only for virus-negative inflammatory CMP (e.g., giant cell, eosinophilic, sarcoid, lupus)

non_pharmacological: Avoid dehydration; most recreational exercise now allowed with shared decision-making
Risk stratify for SCD (HCM Risk-SCD / AHA calculator); family screening and genetic testing
Septal reduction therapy (surgical myectomy preferred; alcohol septal ablation alternative) for drug-refractory obstructive symptoms

pharmacological.regimen: Beta-blocker or verapamil for symptoms (avoid verapamil with severe obstruction/hypotension); discontinue vasodilators and high-dose diuretics in obstructive HCM
Add disopyramide with AV-nodal blocker for obstructive HCM; mavacamten (cardiac myosin inhibitor) for symptomatic obstructive HCM (EXPLORER-HCM/VALOR-HCM)
ICD based on risk factors (massive hypertrophy >=30 mm, unexplained syncope, NSVT, family SCD, abnormal BP response, EF <50%, apical aneurysm)

non_pharmacological: Cautious diuresis; avoid high-dose beta-blockers, verapamil/diltiazem and digoxin (poorly tolerated)
Screen for carpal tunnel, spinal stenosis, neuropathy; genetic testing for hereditary ATTR; screen family

pharmacological.regimen: Tafamidis 61 mg daily (ATTR-ACT mortality benefit) for wild-type or hereditary ATTR with NYHA I-III; inotersen/vutrisiran mainly for hereditary polyneuropathy
Hematology-directed chemotherapy: daratumumab + bortezomib/cyclophosphamide/dexamethasone (ANDROMEDA)
Loop diuretics +/- mineralocorticoid antagonist; midodrine for hypotension; anticoagulate AF regardless of score (high thromboembolic risk)

non_pharmacological: Avoid endurance/competitive exercise (slows disease progression)
Family screening and genetic testing

pharmacological.regimen: Beta-blocker; antiarrhythmics (sotalol or amiodarone) for VT
ICD for sustained VT/VF, severe RV/LV dysfunction or high-risk profile
Catheter ablation for recurrent VT; HF therapy and transplant if end-stage

non_pharmacological: Restrict exercise until symptoms resolve and CRP normalizes
Troponin elevation/echo/MRI to exclude myopericarditis; admit high-risk features (fever >38, subacute, effusion/tamponade, immunosuppression, trauma, OAC use, NSAID failure)

pharmacological.regimen: NSAID (aspirin 500-1000 mg TID or ibuprofen 600 mg TID, taper over weeks) PLUS colchicine 0.5 mg once/twice daily for 3 months (weight-based; COPE/ICAP trials)
Low-dose corticosteroid only if NSAID/colchicine contraindicated or specific immune cause; taper slowly (recurrence risk)
Colchicine 6 months; anakinra (AIRTRIP) or IVIG for colchicine-resistant; rilonacept (RHAPSODY) in approved settings; pericardiectomy last resort

non_pharmacological: Urgent echocardiography; avoid positive-pressure ventilation and diuretics in tamponade (preload dependent)
Pericardiocentesis (echo-guided) is definitive for tamponade; surgical drainage for purulent, loculated or malignant effusions

pharmacological.regimen: IV fluids/volume expansion and vasopressors as bridge to drainage
Anti-TB therapy for tuberculous pericarditis (steroids selective), chemotherapy for malignant, NSAID/colchicine for inflammatory, drainage + antibiotics for purulent

non_pharmacological: No competitive sport for 3-6 months (until normal echo/Holter/troponin)
Cardiac MRI for diagnosis; endomyocardial biopsy in fulminant or treatment-refractory cases
Treat HF and arrhythmias per guidelines; mechanical support for fulminant cases

pharmacological.regimen: Standard HFrEF therapy if LV dysfunction; avoid NSAIDs only when significant LV dysfunction/heart failure present
Immunosuppression ONLY for biopsy-proven virus-negative eosinophilic, giant-cell, sarcoid or autoimmune myocarditis; IVIG considered in select pediatric/fulminant viral cases

non_pharmacological: Endocarditis team approach; repeat blood cultures before antibiotics (unless septic shock)
Transesophageal echo for diagnosis
Early surgery indications: heart failure, uncontrolled infection (abscess, fungi, resistant organisms), prevention of embolism with large vegetations
Dental care and antibiotic prophylaxis only for highest-risk patients undergoing high-risk dental procedures

pharmacological.regimen: Acute native valve: vancomycin + ceftriaxone (or flucloxacillin-based per local protocol); add gentamicin selectively; adjust once cultures identify organism (staph: flucloxacillin/nafcillin or cefazolin if MSSA, vancomycin if MRSA; strep: penicillin/ceftriaxone +/- gentamicin; enterococcus: ampicillin + ceftriaxone)
IV therapy 4-6 weeks (2 weeks select uncomplicated right-sided/strep); OPAT with oral step-down acceptable in stable selected cases (POET trial)

non_pharmacological: Bed rest during acute carditis; echo all patients
Secondary prophylaxis is essential to prevent recurrence

pharmacological.regimen: Benzathine penicillin G IM single dose (or 10-day oral penicillin V/amoxicillin)
Aspirin/NSAIDs for arthritis and mild carditis; corticosteroids for severe carditis with heart failure
Benzathine penicillin G IM every 3-4 weeks: 5 years or until age 21 (no carditis), 10 years or until 40 (carditis), lifelong if severe valve disease/surgery

non_pharmacological: Avoid tachycardia triggers (pregnancy, anemia, thyrotoxicosis increase gradient)
Echo surveillance per severity

pharmacological.regimen: Beta-blocker (or rate-limiting CCB) to increase diastolic filling, especially in AF/pregnancy
Warfarin for AF or prior embolism (DOACs not validated in moderate-severe rheumatic MS)
Percutaneous mitral balloon commissurotomy if favorable valve anatomy and symptomatic severe MS; surgery otherwise

non_pharmacological: Echo surveillance; dental care; treat AF and HTN

pharmacological.regimen: IV vasodilators (nitroprusside) and inotropes/IABP as bridge to urgent surgery
No medical therapy delays surgery; mitral valve REPAIR indicated when symptomatic or LV dysfunction (EF <=60% or LVESD >=40 mm); repair preferred over replacement
Full GDMT for HF plus CRT if indicated first; transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (MitraClip) for selected symptomatic patients despite OMT (COAPT criteria)

non_pharmacological: Avoid dehydration and excessive vasodilators in severe AS; no heavy isometric exercise if severe
Echo surveillance: severe AS every 6-12 months

pharmacological.regimen: No drug slows progression; treat comorbid HTN cautiously starting low dose (ACEi/ARB now considered safe)
AVR for symptomatic severe AS or EF <50%: surgical AVR (generally <75, low risk, or associated CABG) vs TAVI (generally >=75 or high surgical risk); balloon valvuloplasty as bridge only

non_pharmacological: Serial echo surveillance; avoid heavy isometric exercise if severe
Screen for aortopathy (bicuspid valve, Marfan)

pharmacological.regimen: Vasodilators (nifedipine/ACEi/ARB) for symptomatic severe AR when surgery delayed or HTN; beta-blockers in Marfan to slow aortic growth
AVR when symptomatic, EF <=55%, LVESD >50 mm, or when undergoing other cardiac surgery; aortic root surgery for aneurysm per thresholds (Marfan, bicuspid)

non_pharmacological: Refer to expert PH center; confirm diagnosis by right heart catheterization
Supervised exercise training; pregnancy avoidance (high mortality) and contraception; O2 if hypoxemic; diuretics for RV congestion; vaccination; psychosocial support

pharmacological.regimen: High-dose CCB (only ~5-10% responders)
Initial combination therapy: endothelin receptor antagonist (ambrisentan, macitentan or bosentan) + PDE5 inhibitor (sildenafil or tadalafil) - AMBITION approach
Add selexipag (oral IP agonist) if intermediate risk; add IV epoprostenol or SC/IV treprostinil for high-risk/advanced disease
Lung transplant evaluation; balloon pulmonary angioplasty/PEA reserved for CTEPH not PAH

non_pharmacological: Early ambulation once anticoagulated; graduated compression stockings for residual symptoms (not routine for PTS prevention per ASPIRE/SOX)
Assess provoking factors and recurrence risk to decide duration

pharmacological.regimen: DOAC: apixaban 10 mg BID x7 days then 5 mg BID, or rivaroxaban 15 mg BID x21 days then 20 mg OD (single-drug approach); dabigatran/edoxaban after 5-10 days LMWH
LMWH bridged to warfarin (INR 2-3); cancer-associated DVT: LMWH or DOAC (apixaban/edoxaban/rivaroxaban; caution in unresected GI/GU cancers); pregnancy: LMWH throughout
3 months for provoked; extended (possibly reduced-dose apixaban 2.5 BID / rivaroxaban 10 OD) for unprovoked if bleeding risk acceptable
IVC filter; thrombolysis/thrombectomy only for phlegmasia or selected extensive iliofemoral DVT

non_pharmacological: Risk stratify (PESI/sPESI, RV function, troponin)
Early discharge/home treatment for low-risk PE (Hestia/sPESI 0)

pharmacological.regimen: DOAC as for DVT; LMWH if pregnant or cancer per above

Systemic thrombolysis (alteplase 100 mg over 2 h) unless contraindicated; norepinephrine for shock; surgical embolectomy or catheter-directed therapy if lysis contraindicated/failed; VA-ECMO in selected
Anticoagulate and monitor closely; rescue lysis if deterioration (PEITHO)
Reassess at 3 months for unprovoked PE and CTEPH symptoms (V/Q scan)

non_pharmacological: Lifelong anticoagulation
Refer to expert CTEPH center for operability assessment

pharmacological.regimen: Pulmonary endarterectomy (potentially curative) - treatment of choice
Riociguat (CHEST-1); balloon pulmonary angioplasty; add-on PAH therapies in expert centers

non_pharmacological: Smoking cessation (most important)
Supervised exercise therapy 30-45 min sessions, >=3x/week for >=12 weeks
Foot care especially in diabetes; revascularization for lifestyle-limiting claudication after exercise therapy, or urgently for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (rest pain/ulcer)

pharmacological.regimen: Antiplatelet: clopidogrel 75 mg or aspirin; high-intensity statin (atorvastatin 40-80); ACEi/ARB; treat diabetes to target
Rivaroxaban 2.5 mg BID + aspirin after revascularization or in high-risk stable PAD (COMPASS/VOYAGER)
Cilostazol 100 mg BID for claudication (contraindicated in heart failure); naftidrofuryl alternative in some regions
Urgent revascularization (endovascular or bypass) + statin/antiplatelet; antibiotics only if infection

non_pharmacological: Compression stockings (class II) for symptoms/edema/ulcers
Leg elevation, regular calf-muscle exercise, weight loss, avoid prolonged standing
Duplex ultrasound mapping before intervention; ablation/sclerotherapy/surgery for symptomatic or complicated veins; compression + dressings or venous ulcer surgery

pharmacological.regimen: Venoactive drugs (micronized purified flavonoid fraction/MPFF, horse chestnut extract) for symptoms; pentoxifylline + compression for venous ulcers

non_pharmacological: Smoking cessation (slows growth)
Ultrasound surveillance: 3.0-3.9 cm yearly, 4.0-4.9 cm every 3 months, 5.0-5.4 cm every 3 months; men screened at 65 in national programs
Repair threshold: >=5.5 cm in men, >=5.0 cm in women, rapid growth (>5 mm/6 months) or symptomatic - EVAR or open repair

pharmacological.regimen: Statin + antiplatelet + antihypertensive for all with AAA (no drug proven to shrink aneurysm)

non_pharmacological: Immediate ICU care; CT angiography; urgent cardiac surgery consultation for type A

pharmacological.regimen: IV beta-blocker first (esmolol or labetalol) to HR <60 and SBP 100-120; add IV vasodilator (nitroprusside/nicardipine) only AFTER beta-blockade; IV opioids for pain
Emergency surgical repair
Medical therapy unless complicated (malperfusion, rupture, rapid expansion) -> TEVAR preferred; lifelong BP control (beta-blocker based) and imaging surveillance

non_pharmacological: Echo at diagnosis, 2 weeks and 6-8 weeks; annual cardiology follow-up if coronary abnormalities
Delay live vaccines 11 months after high-dose IVIG

pharmacological.regimen: IVIG 2 g/kg single infusion ideally within 10 days + aspirin (high-dose anti-inflammatory then low-dose 3-5 mg/kg until afebrile 48 h, continued 6-8 weeks if no coronary changes)
Second IVIG dose or infliximab; corticosteroids as adjunct in high-risk patients (Kobayashi score)
Low-dose aspirin +/- clopidogrel; anticoagulation (warfarin/LMWH) for giant aneurysms

non_pharmacological: Avoid pregnancy in persistent LV dysfunction (high relapse/mortality risk); MDT care
Bromocriptine to suppress lactation considered (BOARD advisory) - with prophylactic anticoagulation if used

pharmacological.regimen: Beta-blocker (metoprolol), hydralazine + nitrates, digoxin and diuretics; AVOID ACEi/ARB/ARNI/MRA in pregnancy; anticoagulate if EF <30-35%
Full HFrEF therapy compatible with breastfeeding (ACEi enalapril/captopril safe, beta-blocker, diuretics); standard four pillars once not pregnant
Mechanical support/transplant if refractory

diseases.key_guideline: ESC 2024 Cardiomyopathy; Heart Failure Association position paper

non_pharmacological: Identify and treat physical/emotional trigger; coronary angiography to exclude ACS
Avoid inotropes if LV outflow tract obstruction present

pharmacological.regimen: Supportive HF care: diuretics, ACEi/ARB, beta-blocker; catecholamine-sparing strategies
ACEi/ARB and beta-blocker for ~12 months until recovery (beta-blockers shown not to prevent recurrence in long-term data but commonly used); physical and psychological rehabilitation

non_pharmacological: Education and reassurance; avoid triggers (dehydration, heat, prolonged standing)
Physical counter-pressure maneuvers (leg crossing, hand grip)
Adequate hydration and salt intake; tilt training; driving assessment

pharmacological.regimen: Usually no drugs needed; midodrine for frequent recurrences; fludrocortisone second choice (POST-II negative overall but used)
Cardioinhibitory syncope age >40 with documented pauses: dual-chamber pacemaker; cardiac pacing/ablation in select asystolic cases

non_pharmacological: Targeted temperature management: prevent fever (<=37.7 C) - routine hypothermia no longer mandated (TTM2); coronary angiography +/- immediate PCI for STEMI or high suspicion of ischemic trigger
Avoid hypoxia and hyperoxia (SpO2 94-98%), hypotension (MAP >65), and hypoglycemia
Delayed, multimodal neuroprognostication (>=72 h after rewarming/sedation)

pharmacological.regimen: Norepinephrine +/- dobutamine to maintain perfusion; treat seizures with levetiracetam/propofol
Post-MI regimen; ICD if survivor of VF/VT arrest without reversible cause

non_pharmacological: Smoking cessation and avoid second-hand smoke
Regular physical activity; weight loss if obese
Identify/avoid triggers (allergens, NSAIDs if sensitive, occupational sensitizers)
Inhaler technique check and adherence at every visit; written asthma action plan
Treat comorbidities: rhinitis, GERD, OSA, obesity, anxiety
Annual influenza vaccination

pharmacological.regimen: As-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol for symptom relief (reduces severe exacerbations vs SABA-only)
Low-dose ICS-formoterol maintenance AND reliever (MART), or low-dose maintenance ICS-LABA with ICS-containing reliever
Medium-dose ICS-formoterol MART; check adherence/technique/triggers before stepping up

Refer for phenotyping: add LAMA (tiotropium); add-on biologics - anti-IgE omalizumab (allergic), anti-IL5/5R mepolizumab/reslizumab/benralizumab (eosinophilic), dupilumab (anti-IL4R), tezepelumab (anti-TSLP, broad); add-on azithromycin in selected adults
Minimize oral corticosteroids; bronchial thermoplasty in selected centers
If ICS-formoterol not available: regular ICS or ICS-LABA with SABA reliever; never SABA-only treatment

non_pharmacological: Oxygen to SpO2 93-95%; continuous monitoring
Consider ICU/HDU if life-threatening features (silent chest, exhaustion, altered consciousness, SpO2 <92%)

pharmacological.regimen: High-dose inhaled SABA (salbutamol nebulized or MDI+spacer, back-to-back) + ipratropium bromide for severe attacks + systemic corticosteroid (prednisolone 40-50 mg PO or hydrocortisone IV) started within 1 hour
Nebulized magnesium sulfate 2 g for poor response (or IV MgSO4); IV salbutamol only if inhaled therapy not possible; IV aminophylline not routine
NIV cautiously; intubation by experienced clinician if deteriorating; treat precipitant (infection)

non_pharmacological: Smoking cessation (most effective intervention; offer NRT/varenicline)
Pulmonary rehabilitation for all symptomatic patients
Influenza, pneumococcal and RSV vaccination
Weight management and exercise; treat comorbidities
Long-term oxygen therapy >=15 h/day if PaO2 <=55 mmHg (or 56-59 with cor pulmonale/polycythemia); non-invasive ventilation for select chronic hypercapnic patients

pharmacological.line: Primary spontaneous, small (<2 cm rim) minimally symptomatic

non_pharmacological: Diagnostic thoracentesis for new unexplained effusions (Light's criteria for exudate)

non_pharmacological: Resuscitate conservatively (target Hb ~7-8 g/dL; over-transfusion increases portal pressure)
Endoscopic variceal ligation within 12 h; balloon tamponade only as 24 h bridge; early TIPS in high-risk cirrhotics (Child-Pugh C or B with active bleeding)

pharmacological.regimen: Vasoactive drug started at presentation: terlipressin (where available), octreotide or somatostatin infusion for 2-5 days + prophylactic antibiotic (ceftriaxone 1 g/day max 7 days in advanced cirrhosis)
Non-selective beta-blocker (carvedilol/propranolol/nadolol) + repeat EVL until eradication; TIPS if rebleeding
Medium/large varices: NSBB (carvedilol first-line) or EVL

non_pharmacological: Exclude upper source if hemodynamically significant; colonoscopy after purge when stable
CT angiography if active brisk bleeding; IR embolization; surgery last resort

pharmacological.regimen: Resuscitation and restrictive transfusion; reverse coagulopathy judiciously; no routine TXA
Usually self-limited; endoscopic therapy if active stigmata

non_pharmacological: Aggressive early isotonic fluids (lactated Ringer's preferred) - goal-directed, avoid overload; reassess at 12-24 h
Early oral feeding (low-fat solid diet) as tolerated - no nil-by-mouth dogma; enteral nutrition (oral/NG/NJ) if cannot eat by 3-5 days, preferred over TPN
Gallstone etiology: cholecystectomy during index admission for mild disease; ERCP only with concurrent cholangitis or persistent CBD obstruction
No prophylactic antibiotics; treat complications (necrosis walled-off >=4 weeks; drain step-up approach)

pharmacological.regimen: Paracetamol/NSAIDs then opioids as needed (no evidence against morphine use); epidural in select severe cases
Antibiotics only for proven/suspected infected necrosis (carbapenem, or quinolone + metronidazole); catheter/endoscopic drainage then necrosectomy if needed (PANTER step-up)
Prophylactic antibiotics, protease inhibitors, octreotide, routine ICU antioxidants

non_pharmacological: Absolute alcohol and smoking cessation (both slow progression)
Small low-fat meals; pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT) 40,000-75,000 units lipase with meals for steatorrhea/weight loss
Screen for diabetes (type 3c), osteoporosis, fat-soluble vitamin deficiency; pain psychology support
Endoscopy/surgery for ductal stones/strictures (ESWL + ERCP; lateral pancreaticojejunostomy for dilated duct - surgery superior to endoscopy long term)

pharmacological.regimen: Paracetamol/NSAIDs -> weak opioids (avoid chronic strong opioids) -> pregabalin/antioxidant cocktail (modest benefit); celiac plexus block selected
Add PPI to improve enzyme efficacy; titrate to steatorrhea/weight
Insulin often required; metformin if residual function

non_pharmacological: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy for symptomatic cholelithiasis (definitive; prevents complications)
Asymptomatic stones: observation except porcelain gallbladder, large stones, transplant candidates

pharmacological.regimen: NSAID first-line (diclofenac/ketorolac IM/PO); antispasmodics/opioids if needed
Ursodeoxycholic acid can dissolve small radiolucent stones (high recurrence); rarely used

non_pharmacological: Early laparoscopic cholecystectomy (within 72 h of onset / index admission) for all operable patients
High-risk surgical patients: percutaneous cholecystostomy + antibiotics

pharmacological.regimen: Community-acquired mild-moderate: cefuroxime/ceftriaxone or ampicillin-sulbactam + metronidazole if biliary-enteric manipulation; severe/healthcare-associated: piperacillin-tazobactam or carbapenem; total 4-7 days, or 4 days post-source control (STOP-IT principle); stop 24 h after cholecystectomy for uncomplicated

non_pharmacological: Urgent biliary drainage - ERCP with sphincterotomy and stone extraction (within 24-48 h; emergent if septic shock)
PTBD or surgical drainage if ERCP fails

pharmacological.regimen: Empiric: piperacillin-tazobactam or ceftriaxone + metronidazole (community); carbapenem or pip-tazo if healthcare-associated/severe; tailor to cultures; typical 4-7 days after source control
Sepsis bundle: fluids, cultures, vasopressors as needed

non_pharmacological: Risk stratify (ASGE criteria: EUS/MRCP for intermediate risk, ERCP for high risk)
ERCP with sphincterotomy and extraction; cholecystectomy afterwards to prevent recurrence

pharmacological.regimen: Ursodeoxycholic acid has no acute role; antibiotics only if cholangitis/instrumentation

non_pharmacological: MRCP for diagnosis; screen for IBD (majority have UC)
Cholangiocarcinoma and colorectal cancer surveillance; dilate dominant strictures endoscopically with brushings

pharmacological.regimen: No approved drug; moderate-dose ursodeoxycholic acid (13-23 mg/kg/day) used by many for biochemistry (high-dose harmful); cholestyramine/rifampicin for pruritus; liver transplantation for decompensation/pericular cholangitis; avoid high-dose UDCA
Nor-UDCA, selonsertib etc. in trials (not approved)

non_pharmacological: Diagnose with AMA + cholestatic LFTs; screen thyroid, osteoporosis, fat-soluble vitamins

pharmacological.regimen: Ursodeoxycholic acid 13-15 mg/kg/day lifelong

Obeticholic acid (avoid in decompensated cirrhosis - FDA restriction) or fibrate (bezafibrate/fenofibrate off-label; seladelpar approved 2024 for PBC in adults with inadequate UDCA response/intolerance)
Cholestyramine first; rifampicin second (monitor LFTs); naltrexone/sertraline alternatives
Liver transplantation

non_pharmacological: Diagnosis: IgG, ANA/SMA/LKM antibodies, simplified score; biopsy
Monitor IgG/transaminases; bone protection with steroids

pharmacological.regimen: Prednisone/prednisolone 0.5-1 mg/kg taper + azathioprine added once bilirubin acceptable; budesonide (3 mg TID) + azathioprine for non-cirrhotic mild disease
Azathioprine monotherapy (target normal IgG/transaminases; long-term/indefinite)
Mycophenolate mofetil first rescue; tacrolimus/cyclosporine, rituximab or infliximab in expert centers
IV steroids trial with early transplant center referral (failure by day 7 = transplant listing)

non_pharmacological: Stage disease (HBeAg, HBV DNA, ALT, fibrosis assessment); HCC surveillance ultrasound +/- AFP every 6 months in at-risk
Screen household/sexual contacts and vaccinate; avoid alcohol; screen for HDV/HCV/HIV

pharmacological.regimen: Entecavir, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) or tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) - high barrier to resistance; usually long-term/lifelong
Pegylated interferon alfa 48 weeks in selected HBeAg+ patients (genotype A, high ALT); stop nucleos(t)ide analogues in select HBeAg-negative after sustained response per guidelines
Tenofovir from third trimester if high viral load (>200,000 IU/mL) to prevent vertical transmission; newborn HBV vaccine + HBIG within 12 h
Peg-IFN or bulevirtide (EU-approved entry inhibitor) in specialist care

non_pharmacological: Treat all viremic patients; assess fibrosis (FIB-4/elastography)
Screen for HBV/HIV; avoid alcohol; HCC surveillance if cirrhotic

pharmacological.regimen: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir x8 weeks (treatment-naive without cirrhosis; 12 weeks compensated cirrhosis per some labels) OR sofosbuvir/velpatasvir x12 weeks
Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir + ribavirin x12 weeks (avoid protease inhibitors)
Sofosbuvir/velpatasvir/voxilaprevir x12 weeks; expert salvage otherwise
SVR12 (undetectable RNA 12 weeks post-treatment)

non_pharmacological: Supportive care; hydration; avoid alcohol and hepatotoxins
Contact tracing; vaccination (HAV vaccine for contacts within 2 weeks); notify public health

pharmacological.regimen: Antiemetics, antipyretics; hospitalize for acute liver failure signs (coagulopathy, encephalopathy) -> transplant center

pharmacological.line: Severe/cholestatic HEV or chronic HEV in immunosuppressed
pharmacological.regimen: Ribavirin 12 weeks (reduce immunosuppression first)

non_pharmacological: Treat etiology (alcohol abstinence with support, DAA for HCV, antivirals for HBV, weight loss for MASLD)
HCC surveillance ultrasound +/- AFP every 6 months; variceal screening per Baveno (elastography + platelets can defer)
Vaccinate (HAV, HBV, influenza, pneumococcal); avoid NSAIDs; limit paracetamol to 2 g/day; protein NOT restricted (1.2-1.5 g/kg); coffee may be beneficial

pharmacological.regimen: Carvedilol/NSBB when clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH) to prevent decompensation (Baveno VII)
Late-evening snack; vitamin supplementation; treat sarcopenia with exercise

diseases.key_guideline: EASL/AASLD decompensated and compensated cirrhosis guidance

non_pharmacological: Sodium restriction 2 g/day; diagnostic paracentesis for all new ascites/admissions (exclude SBP)
Fluid restriction only if Na <125-128; stop NSAIDs, vasodilators where possible
Large-volume paracentesis (>5 L) with albumin 8 g/L removed

pharmacological.regimen: Spironolactone 100 mg + furosemide 40 mg daily, titrate every 3-5 days (max 400/160); spironolactone alone if mild
Serial LVP + albumin; midodrine in hypotensive cirrhotics; TIPS in selected (watch encephalopathy); liver transplant evaluation
ACEi/ARB in advanced cirrhosis with hypotension

non_pharmacological: Diagnostic paracentesis: PMN >=250/mm3 = treat empirically without waiting for culture
IV albumin 1.5 g/kg day 1 and 1 g/kg day 3 if Cr >1, BUN >30 or bilirubin >4 (SORT trial)

pharmacological.regimen: IV cefotaxime 2 g q8h (or ceftriaxone) for 5-7 days; broaden (piperacillin-tazobactam/carbapenem) for nosocomial or septic shock
Daily norfloxacin (400 mg) or TMP-SMX DS or ciprofloxacin indefinitely until transplant/resolution
Consider in ascitic protein <1.5 g/dL with renal/liver dysfunction

non_pharmacological: Search precipitants: infection (SBP, UTI), GI bleed, constipation, electrolytes, dehydration, sedatives, TIPS
Maintain protein intake 1.2-1.5 g/kg/day (vegetable/dairy favored); do NOT chronically restrict protein

pharmacological.regimen: Lactulose titrated to 2-3 soft stools/day (oral or enema if obtunded)
Rifaximin 550 mg BID added after >=2 episodes (or intolerance); continue lactulose
Consider LOLA (L-ornithine L-aspartate), zinc if deficient; evaluate/revise TIPS; albumin infusions emerging evidence
Rifaximin or lactulose considered to prevent progression/driving impairment

non_pharmacological: Exclude other AKI causes; stop diuretics/nephrotoxins; volume expand with albumin 1 g/kg x2 days for diagnosis
ICU for type 1; early transplant evaluation (HRS can reverse post-transplant)

pharmacological.regimen: Terlipressin (2-12 mg/day IV) + IV albumin (20-40 g/day) - CONFIRM trial; norepinephrine + albumin in ICU alternative; midodrine + octreotide if terlipressin unavailable
RRT if needed; TIPS selected cases; liver transplant definitive

non_pharmacological: Complete alcohol abstinence + addiction support (cornerstone of long-term survival)
Nutrition: high-calorie/high-protein enteral feeding; exclude infection (panculture); assess severity with Maddrey DF and MELD

pharmacological.regimen: Prednisolone 40 mg/day x28 days after excluding contraindications; Lille score at day 7 to continue/stop (STOPAH); N-acetylcysteine IV adjunct may improve 1-month survival
Nutrition + abstinence; pentoxifylline no longer recommended
Acamprosate, naltrexone (caution if LFTs very elevated), baclofen (safe in liver disease); early liver transplant protocols for highly selected

non_pharmacological: Weight loss target >=7-10% (diet + exercise) resolves steatohepatitis/fibrosis in many; bariatric surgery if eligible
Treat metabolic comorbidities (T2D, dyslipidemia, HTN); coffee; avoid alcohol excess
Fibrosis risk stratification with FIB-4/elastography; HCC surveillance only if cirrhosis

pharmacological.regimen: GLP-1 receptor agonists (semaglutide) improve steatohepatitis (especially with diabetes/obesity); resmetirom (thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonist) FDA-approved 2024 for non-cirrhotic MASH with F2-F3 fibrosis
Pioglitazone (with/without diabetes, biopsy-proven MASH); SGLT2 inhibitors for metabolic benefit
Vitamin E 800 IU/day option in non-diabetic non-cirrhotic biopsy-proven MASH; statins safe and indicated for CVD risk; bariatric surgery
Manage complications; transplant; pioglitazone/resmetirom not in decompensation

non_pharmacological: Stop suspected agent immediately (most important); review all drugs/herbals (green tea extract, kava, bodybuilding supplements, amoxicillin-clavulanate, isoniazid, valproate, methotrexate common)
Hy's law (ALT >3x ULN + bilirubin >2x ULN without obstruction) predicts severe outcome; report to pharmacovigilance

pharmacological.regimen: N-acetylcysteine for paracetamol toxicity (and consider in non-paracetamol acute liver failure); L-carnitine for valproate; ursodeoxycholic acid sometimes for cholestatic DILI; corticosteroids only for DILI with autoimmune features or DRESS
Early transplant center referral (King's College criteria)

non_pharmacological: HFE genotyping in relatives; avoid iron supplements, excess vitamin C with meals, raw shellfish (Vibrio)
Monitor ferritin and transferrin saturation

pharmacological.regimen: Phlebotomy: 450-500 mL weekly/biweekly until ferritin 50-100 ug/L, then maintenance 2-6x/year
Iron chelation (deferasirox/deferoxamine) off-label
Manage cirrhosis/HCC risk; arthropathy/endocrinopathy supportive

non_pharmacological: Lifelong treatment; screen siblings; avoid copper-rich foods (shellfish, liver, mushrooms, chocolate) initially; ophthalmology slit-lamp for KF rings
Monitor 24-h urinary copper and free copper

pharmacological.regimen: Chelation: trientine (preferred first-line now in many centers) or D-penicillamine (with pyridoxine) - never stop treatment
Zinc salts (blocks intestinal absorption); trientine maintenance alternative
Start zinc or trientine cautiously (penicillamine may worsen neuro symptoms)
Liver transplantation (curative)

non_pharmacological: Anticoagulation for all; investigate myeloproliferative neoplasm (JAK2) and prothrombotic states
Stepwise approach: anticoagulation -> angioplasty/stenting of short stenoses -> TIPS -> liver transplant

pharmacological.regimen: Full anticoagulation (LMWH bridging to warfarin INR 2-3 or DOAC per evidence) + treat ascites (diuretics/sodium restriction)
Cytoreduction (hydroxyurea/ruxolitinib) per hematology

non_pharmacological: Increase fiber gradually (25 g/day), fluids, regular exercise, toileting routine with footstool (squatty posture)
Exclude red flags, medications (opioids, anticholinergics), hypothyroidism, hypercalcemia; anorectal physiology if outlet dysfunction; pelvic floor biofeedback for dyssynergia

pharmacological.regimen: Bulk-forming fiber (psyllium) then osmotic laxatives (PEG/macrogol first-line pharmacologic; lactulose alternative)
Stimulant laxatives (bisacodyl/senna) as needed or short-term regular
Secretagogues/prokinetics: lubiprostone, linaclotide, plecanatide, prucalopride (5-HT4 agonist); tenapanor
Same ladder; add peripherally acting mu-opioid antagonists (methylnaltrexone, naloxegol) if refractory
Biofeedback first; suppositories/enemas; surgery rare

non_pharmacological: Digital disimpaction if rectal; enemas (saline/mineral oil) then PEG lavage
Prevention program after clearance

pharmacological.regimen: High-dose PEG (e.g., 2-4 L/day) or suppositories/enemas; avoid bulk fiber until cleared
Daily osmotic laxative + stimulant as needed; address causes (opioids, immobility)

non_pharmacological: High-fiber diet; regular exercise; weight control (nuts/seeds restriction NOT required)
Colonoscopy after bleeding episode to exclude malignancy

pharmacological.regimen: Usually self-limited; supportive; endoscopic therapy if active stigmata; mesalamine/antibiotics NOT indicated for asymptomatic diverticulosis

non_pharmacological: CT abdomen/pelvis for diagnosis and complications
Uncomplicated: selective outpatient management WITHOUT routine antibiotics in immunocompetent mild cases (DINAMO/AVOD trials)
Colonoscopy 6-8 weeks after complicated/first episode if not recently done; elective resection individualized (no longer based on episode count)

pharmacological.regimen: Oral amoxicillin-clavulanate or ciprofloxacin + metronidazole for 4-7 days
IV piperacillin-tazobactam, or ceftriaxone + metronidazole; percutaneous drainage if abscess >3-4 cm; emergency surgery for diffuse peritonitis
No proven medical prophylaxis (mesalamine/rifaximin not recommended); diet/exercise; elective sigmoid colectomy for immunosuppressed or frequent burdensome episodes

non_pharmacological: CT/ultrasound diagnosis; early laparoscopic appendectomy remains standard of care
Antibiotics-first strategy acceptable for selected uncomplicated appendicitis with shared decision-making (CODA/APPAC: ~30-40% recurrence by 1 year)

pharmacological.regimen: Single-dose broad-spectrum antibiotic (cefazolin + metronidazole, or ceftriaxone + metronidazole, or ampicillin-sulbactam)
IV antibiotics then oral course (e.g., ceftriaxone + metronidazole, or amoxicillin-clavulanate) total ~7-10 days; interval appendectomy not routine
Percutaneous drainage + IV antibiotics; interval appendectomy individualized

non_pharmacological: NPO, NG decompression, IV fluids, electrolyte correction
CT to identify closed-loop/strangulation - immediate surgery if ischemia, virgin abdomen without hernia, or complete obstruction not resolving in 48-72 h
Adhesive SBO: non-operative trial with water-soluble contrast (Gastrografin) diagnostic and therapeutic

pharmacological.regimen: Analgesia, antiemetics; antibiotics only if strangulation/surgery
Octreotide, antisecretory (hyoscine), dexamethasone, metoclopramide if partial; venting gastrostomy/stents in selected

non_pharmacological: CT + colonoscopy (non-inflated) for diagnosis; IV fluids, bowel rest, optimize perfusion
Avoid vasoconstrictors/constipating drugs; surgery if peritonitis/gangrene

pharmacological.regimen: Broad-spectrum antibiotics (cover translocation); manage underlying low-flow state, AF embolism
Different entity - emergent CTA; immediate anticoagulation + revascularization (endovascular first for embolus, surgery if peritonitis); antibiotics; high mortality

diseases.key_guideline: ACG 2015 colonic ischemia; WSES mesenteric ischemia

non_pharmacological: Multidisciplinary intestinal rehabilitation; dietitian (complex carbs, oxalate restriction if colon-in-continuity; small frequent meals, sips between meals)
Monitor for D-lactic acidosis, gallstones, renal oxalate stones, bone disease

pharmacological.regimen: High-dose PPI initially; loperamide/diphenoxylate; octreotide selected
Parenteral nutrition (lipid-sparing strategies); teduglutide (GLP-2 analog) to enhance absorption and wean PN
Intestinal lengthening procedures; intestinal transplant for PN failure/complications

non_pharmacological: Consider after cholecystectomy, ileal resection, or idiopathic; SeHCAT scan where available or empiric trial

pharmacological.regimen: Bile acid sequestrants: cholestyramine powder (palatability issue), colesevelam (better tolerated) or colestipol
Loperamide adjunct; treat ileal Crohn's if present

non_pharmacological: Fiber (psyllium) and fluids; avoid straining/prolonged sitting; sitz baths
Office procedures for grade I-III: rubber band ligation (most effective), sclerotherapy, infrared coagulation; hemorrhoidectomy for large/refractory (grade IV, thrombosed external <72 h)

pharmacological.regimen: Topical anesthetics/steroid creams short-term (<=7 days); flavonoids (MPFF) reduce bleeding episodes; stool softeners
Excision within 72 h; analgesia otherwise

non_pharmacological: Stool softeners + fiber + sitz baths first-line
Lateral internal sphincterotomy for chronic refractory (gold standard surgical cure; small incontinence risk); Botox alternative

pharmacological.regimen: Topical GTN 0.2-0.4% ointment or diltiazem 2% / nifedipine ointment BID x6-8 weeks (headache limits GTN)

non_pharmacological: Incision and drainage for abscess (antibiotics alone insufficient)
MRI pelvis for complex/recurrent tracts; exclude Crohn's, TB, malignancy

pharmacological.regimen: Fistulotomy after drainage (low tracts)
Seton placement + infliximab-based Crohn's therapy; LIFT/advancement flap for high tracts; antibiotics (ciprofloxacin/metronidazole) adjunct only

non_pharmacological: Acute abscess: incision and drainage
Chronic: hair removal (shaving/laser), hygiene; off-midline closure (Karydakis/Bascom cleft lift) preferred over midline excision

pharmacological.regimen: Antibiotics only for surrounding cellulitis/immunosuppression

non_pharmacological: Multimodal ERAS: early feeding, early mobilization, opioid-sparing analgesia, avoid NG routine, gum chewing
Correct electrolytes (K+, Mg2+); exclude mechanical obstruction

pharmacological.regimen: Alvimopan (perioperative mu-opioid antagonist, US); minimize opioids (epidural/local infiltration); no benefit from routine metoclopramide/erythromycin in postop ileus
Conservative 24-48 h if cecum <12 cm; neostigmine 2 mg IV with cardiac monitoring if failing; colonoscopic decompression; avoid neostigmine in bradycardia/bronchospasm

non_pharmacological: Differentiate from Crohn's (biopsy, culture, PCR, IGRA, imaging); surgery for perforation, obstruction, hemorrhage

pharmacological.regimen: Standard anti-TB regimen 2RHZE/4RH (extend to 9 months in select/abdominal per some guidelines); steroids not routine except peritoneal with adhesions/severe toxemia (weak evidence)

diseases.disease: Acute cholangitis (see) / biliary strictures / post-cholecystectomy syndrome
non_pharmacological: Structured workup: LFTs, EUS/MRCP, manometry if sphincter of Oddi dysfunction suspected
Retained stones: ERCP

pharmacological.regimen: Antispasmodics, PPI if dyspepsia; sphincterotomy for documented sphincter of Oddi dysfunction (now rarely performed; Rome IV criteria favor functional pain approach)

non_pharmacological: Small frequent meals; separate liquids from solids by 30 min; avoid simple sugars; add complex carbs, protein, fiber; lie down after meals

pharmacological.regimen: Acarbose with meals (late dumping); pectin/guar gum thickeners
Octreotide SC TID (or long-acting monthly); diazoxide rarely for hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia
Surgical revision in expert centers

diseases.key_guideline: Endocrine Society post-bariatric hypoglycemia; UpToDate consensus

non_pharmacological: Acute: supportive (diarrhea management); chronic bleeding: endoscopic argon plasma coagulation first-line

pharmacological.regimen: Loperamide, hydration; sucralfate enemas; consider probiotics during pelvic RT
Sucralfate enemas; formalin application or APC endoscopically; hyperbaric oxygen for refractory

non_pharmacological: Resection for localized disease; mutational testing (KIT/PDGFRA) guides therapy

pharmacological.regimen: Imatinib 400 mg x3 years
Imatinib 400 mg first-line; sunitinib second-line; regorafenib third-line; ripretinib fourth-line; avapritinib for PDGFRA D842V mutation

non_pharmacological: Resection/localized therapies where possible; somatostatin receptor imaging (Ga-68 DOTATATE PET)

pharmacological.regimen: Somatostatin analogs (octreotide LAR/lanreotide) first-line for well-differentiated SSTR+ midgut NET (PROMID/CLARINET)
Everolimus (RADIANT trials); peptide receptor radionuclide therapy Lu-177-DOTATATE (NETTER-1) for SSTR+ midgut
Sunitinib or everolimus; CAPTEM chemotherapy for bulky pancreatic NET; carcinoid syndrome: SSA + telotristat for refractory diarrhea

non_pharmacological: Stage by KDIGO; search for reversible causes: volume status, obstruction (bladder scan/US), sepsis, nephrotoxins
Stop NSAIDs, ACEi/ARB during acute illness, aminoglycosides, IV contrast where possible
Renal ultrasound to exclude obstruction; strict fluid balance, daily weights
RRT indications: refractory acidosis, hyperkalemia, intoxication, overload, uremic complications

pharmacological.regimen: Volume repletion with balanced crystalloids (avoid HES; albumin in cirrhosis/nephrotic); vasopressors (norepinephrine) if septic shock
Treat cause (ATN supportive; GN per specific disease; AIN - stop culprit, consider steroids if no recovery); rhabdomyolysis: aggressive fluids
Catheter, ureteric stents or nephrostomy for obstruction
Manage hyperkalemia (insulin-dextrose, calcium, dialysis), acidosis (bicarbonate if severe), pulmonary edema (loop diuretics/dialysis)
Diuretics to prevent/treat AKI (except overload); dopamine; fenoldopam

diseases.key_guideline: KDIGO AKI 2012 (2024 update in progress); Surviving Sepsis 2024

non_pharmacological: BP target <130/80 (or SBP <120 by standardized measurement per KDIGO 2024); low-sodium diet
Protein ~0.8 g/kg/day in non-dialysis CKD; avoid nephrotoxins; smoking cessation
Cardiovascular risk management (statin if age >=50); dose-adjust all drugs by eGFR
Dialysis access planning at G4; transplant referral/pre-emptive transplant preferred at G5

pharmacological.regimen: ACEi or ARB titrated to max tolerated (expect <=30% creatinine rise); SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin/empagliflozin) for eGFR >=20 with albuminuria or T2D (DAPA-CKD/EMPA-KIDNEY); finerenone for T2D-associated CKD with albuminuria despite RASi (FIDELIO/FIGARO)
GLP-1 RA in T2D with CKD; statin +/- ezetimibe; BP add-ons: dihydropyridine CCB, thiazide-like (chlorthalidone works to eGFR ~20-30), loop diuretics in G4-5

Metabolic acidosis: oral bicarbonate to keep HCO3 >=22; anemia: IV/PO iron, ESA targeting Hb 10-11.5 g/dL (avoid >13), HIF-PH inhibitors (daprodustat etc.) where approved; hyperphosphatemia: phosphate binders (calcium-based, sevelamer, lanthanum) + dietary restriction; secondary hyperparathyroidism: vitamin D, calcimimetics (cinacalcet)
HD: phosphate binders, ESA, vitamin D analogs; PD: peritonitis protocols

non_pharmacological: Annual UACR + eGFR screening; BP <130/80; sodium <2 g/day; protein 0.8 g/kg/day; smoking cessation

pharmacological.regimen: ACEi/ARB for albuminuria (UACR >=30); SGLT2 inhibitor (canagliflozin CREDENCE, dapagliflozin DAPA-CKD, empagliflozin EMPA-KIDNEY) - foundation therapy
Finerenone (non-steroidal MRA) on top of ACEi/ARB + SGLT2i if persistent albuminuria and K+ allows
Individualized HbA1c ~7%; GLP-1 RA for additional glycemic/CV benefit; metformin to eGFR 30

non_pharmacological: Salt restriction; edema management; VTE risk assessment (albumin <2.0-2.5 consider prophylactic anticoagulation)
Exclude secondary causes (NSAIDs, lymphoma, atopy); biopsy atypical features in adults

pharmacological.regimen: Oral prednisone 1 mg/kg/day (max 80) until remission then taper over 4-6+ months (KDIGO 2024 recommends longer tapers to reduce relapse); children: 12-week per ISKDC or 6-month schedules
Steroid-sparing: tacrolimus/cyclosporine, mycophenolate, rituximab (increasingly favored in children), or cyclophosphamide
Calcineurin inhibitor + genetic testing; consider alternate diagnosis (FSGS)
Loop diuretics +/- albumin infusion for severe edema; ACEi/ARB to reduce proteinuria; statins if persistent; avoid NSAIDs

non_pharmacological: Distinguish primary (biopsy + nephrotic syndrome) from secondary (adaptive: obesity, reduced nephron mass; viral: HIV, parvovirus; drugs: pamidronate, anabolic steroids)
Secondary FSGS: treat cause (weight loss, HIV ART) - do NOT use steroids

pharmacological.regimen: High-dose glucocorticoids (prednisone 1 mg/kg, prolonged course up to 16 weeks before declaring resistance)
Calcineurin inhibitor (cyclosporine/tacrolimus) >=6 months; add low-dose steroid
Rituximab, mycophenolate, or adrenocorticotropic hormone gel (selected); recurrent FSGS post-transplant: plasmapheresis + rituximab/abatacept (expert)
ACEi/ARB, SGLT2i, diuretics, statin

non_pharmacological: Anti-PLA2R antibody testing for primary disease; exclude secondary causes (malignancy screening in older adults, lupus, HBV, drugs)
Supportive first for all: RAAS blockade, BP control, edema management, statin, VTE prophylaxis if high risk

pharmacological.regimen: Low risk: supportive 6 months; moderate risk: rituximab OR cyclosporine/tacrolimus + low-dose steroid; high/very high risk (declining kidney function, severe nephrotic syndrome): rituximab first-line OR cyclical alkylating agent (cyclophosphamide) + glucocorticoid (Ponticelli regimen) OR calcineurin inhibitor
Serial anti-PLA2R titers to assess response; avoid prolonged high-dose steroids alone (insufficient)

non_pharmacological: Kidney biopsy for diagnosis; risk stratify by proteinuria, eGFR slope, MEST score

pharmacological.regimen: Optimized supportive care >=3 months: max-tolerated ACEi/ARB + SGLT2 inhibitor (DAPA-CKD/EMPA-KIDNEY support) aiming proteinuria <0.5-1 g/day
Targeted-release budesonide (Nefecon/Tarpeyo) 16 mg/day x9 months (NefIgArd); or 6-month corticosteroid course with infection prophylaxis (TESTING reduced-dose protocol) - weigh infection risk
Sparsentan (dual endothelin/angiotensin receptor antagonist) FDA-approved 2023 to reduce proteinuria; iptacopan and other complement inhibitors in late trials
Treat like ANCA vasculitis: steroids + cyclophosphamide

non_pharmacological: Supportive: salt/water restriction, diuretics, BP control
Treat ongoing infection (penicillin for strep); complement and ASO/anti-DNase B titers; biopsy if atypical

pharmacological.regimen: Penicillin/amoxicillin for GAS; appropriate antibiotics for staph/other
Not indicated for typical post-streptococcal GN; steroids only for crescentic/rapidly progressive biopsy-proven disease

non_pharmacological: Kidney biopsy with ISN/RPS class + activity/chronicity; hydroxychloroquine for ALL SLE patients unless contraindicated
BP target <130/80; RAAS blockade for proteinuria; SLE pregnancy planning (stable 6 months)

MMF (preferred) or azathioprine + low-dose steroid; belimumab or voclosporin continuation options

pharmacological.line: Pure class V with nephrotic proteinuria
pharmacological.regimen: MMF or CNI-based; RAAS blockade

Proteinuria, complements, anti-dsDNA at each visit

non_pharmacological: Biopsy/serology (PR3/MPO); exclude infection before escalation; PJP prophylaxis with immunosuppression

Stop offending drugs (ACEi/ARB/spironolactone/TMP/NSAIDs if feasible); low-K diet, loop/thiazide diuretics, fludrocortisone if hypoaldosteronism; oral bicarbonate if acidemic

non_pharmacological: Fluid intake to achieve urine volume >=2.5 L/day
Normal dietary calcium (do NOT restrict; 1000-1200 mg/day), sodium <2.3 g/day, moderate animal protein
24-hour urine metabolic evaluation in recurrent/high-risk stone formers; strain stones for analysis

Allopurinol; purine restriction

ESWL, ureteroscopy or PCNL by size/location

non_pharmacological: Uric acid stones: alkalinize urine (pH 7.0-7.2) - can chemolyse; hydration; purine restriction
Cystine: fluid intake >3 L/day, sodium and animal protein restriction
Struvite: infection stones - complete removal required

pharmacological.regimen: Potassium citrate; allopurinol/febuxostat for hyperuricosuria/hyperuricemia
Potassium citrate; tiopronin (or D-penicillamine) if conservative measures fail
Complete surgical clearance + culture-directed antibiotics; acetohydroxamic acid rarely (side effects)

pharmacological.regimen: Nitrofurantoin 100 mg BID x5 days OR TMP-SMX DS BID x3 days OR fosfomycin 3 g single dose
Beta-lactams (cefalexin, amoxicillin-clavulanate) 5-7 days; reserve fluoroquinolones for when no alternatives

diseases.key_guideline: IDSA 2011 (still referenced); EAU 2024; AUA/SUFU 2022 recurrent UTI

non_pharmacological: Urine culture before antibiotics; image (US/CT) if no improvement by 48-72 h (abscess, obstruction)
Admit if septic, vomiting, pregnancy, obstruction, immunosuppressed

pharmacological.regimen: Oral ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID x7 days or levofloxacin 750 mg x5 days; TMP-SMX x14 days if susceptible; initial IV ceftriaxone dose if local FQ resistance >10%
IV ceftriaxone or piperacillin-tazobactam; de-escalate per culture; carbapenem if ESBL risk
7 days FQ, 10-14 days beta-lactam/TMP-SMX; longer for abscess

non_pharmacological: Prevent: avoid/early removal of catheter, closed drainage, aseptic insertion
Do NOT treat asymptomatic bacteriuria (except pregnancy, before urologic procedures)

non_pharmacological: Urine culture + blood cultures; avoid urethral catheterization (use suprapubic if retention); STI testing in young

pharmacological.regimen: Fluoroquinolone (ciprofloxacin/levofloxacin) or TMP-SMX for 2-4 weeks (good prostatic penetration); IV broad-spectrum (piperacillin-tazobactam) if septic; ceftriaxone + doxycycline if gonococcal/chlamydial
Tamsulosin adjunct for voiding symptoms; abscess: transrectal/perineal drainage

diseases.disease: Chronic prostatitis / chronic pelvic pain syndrome
non_pharmacological: Phenotype-directed multimodal therapy (UPOINT)
Pelvic floor physiotherapy; stress management; avoid prolonged sitting triggers

pharmacological.regimen: Alpha-blocker x6-12 weeks (especially voiding symptoms); short NSAID course; if inflammatory: quercetin or pollen extract (evidence modest)
Amitriptyline, duloxetine, pregabalin/gabapentin; myofascial trigger point therapy
Repeated long antibiotic courses without proven infection

non_pharmacological: Mild symptoms: watchful waiting - reduce evening fluids, caffeine/alcohol moderation, double voiding, review drugs (decongestants, anticholinergics)
IPSS scoring; PSA and DRE; urodynamics/post-void residual if surgery contemplated

pharmacological.regimen: Alpha-1 blocker (tamsulosin, alfuzosin, silodosin) for rapid relief

Tadalafil 5 mg daily
TURP, laser enucleation (HoLEP), Rezum/UroLift/PAE in selected; retention, recurrent UTI, stones, renal failure = surgical indications

non_pharmacological: Cardiovascular risk assessment (ED can precede CAD); lifestyle: weight loss, exercise, smoking cessation
Psychogenic component: psychosexual therapy; review drugs (SSRIs, beta-blockers, finasteride)

pharmacological.regimen: PDE5 inhibitor (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil, avanafil) - contraindicated with nitrates/riociguat
Only if confirmed hypogonadism (may augment PDE5i response)
Intracavernosal injection (alprostadil or Trimix), intraurethral alprostadil, vacuum erection device
Penile prosthesis; penile revascularization in select young trauma patients

non_pharmacological: Bladder retraining, pelvic floor exercises, fluid/caffeine moderation, weight loss (first-line for all)

pharmacological.regimen: Beta-3 agonist (mirabegron/vibegron - preferred, fewer cognitive effects) or antimuscarinic (solifenacin, oxybutynin, tolterodine; avoid oxybutynin in elderly/cognitive impairment)
Mirabegron + solifenacin if monotherapy insufficient
Intravesical onabotulinumtoxinA 100U, percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation, or sacral neuromodulation

non_pharmacological: Education; dietary trigger avoidance (caffeine, alcohol, citrus, spicy)
Pelvic floor physiotherapy (myofascial release); stress management; cystoscopy optional (Hunner lesions: fulguration/triamcinolone injection)

pharmacological.regimen: Amitriptyline (start 10 mg, titrate) and/or pentosan polysulfate (counsel on rare maculopathy and need for ophthalmic screening)
Intravesical DMSO instillations; intravesical heparin/lidocaine
Cyclosporine A; sacral neuromodulation not for pain; avoid chronic antibiotics and repeated hydrodistension
Cystectomy with urinary diversion in intractable, carefully selected cases

non_pharmacological: Scrotal elevation, ice, rest; exclude torsion (Doppler if any doubt)
STI testing in sexually active <35; urine culture in older men

pharmacological.regimen: Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM + doxycycline 100 mg BID x10 days; add levofloxacin x10 days if insertive anal sex (enteric coverage)
Levofloxacin 500 mg x10 days or TMP-SMX
NSAIDs; admission if sepsis/abscess (drainage)

non_pharmacological: SURGICAL EMERGENCY - do not delay for imaging if high suspicion; salvage rate drops markedly after 6 h
Contralateral orchidopexy at same surgery

pharmacological.regimen: Analgesia; manual detorsion ('open the book') as temporizing measure only; antibiotics if necrosis/infection

non_pharmacological: Identify cause (stone, stricture, tumor, retroperitoneal fibrosis, pregnancy)
Decompress if infected, bilateral, solitary kidney, or renal function declining: retrograde stent or percutaneous nephrostomy

pharmacological.regimen: Stone management (see urolithiasis); steroids/tamoxifen for idiopathic retroperitoneal fibrosis (with ureteral stenting); treat malignancy

non_pharmacological: Renal stones <20 mm: ESWL or flexible ureteroscopy; >20 mm or lower pole >10 mm: PCNL preferred
Ureteric stones: ureteroscopy or ESWL; stent pre-treatment optional
Emergency drainage if sepsis with obstruction

pharmacological.regimen: Perioperative antibiotics per culture; alpha-blockers after ureteroscopy for stent discomfort; repeat metabolic prevention long-term

non_pharmacological: Imaging follow-up for residual fragments; metabolic evaluation
All stone formers: fluids, diet; targeted pharmacotherapy per 24-h urine (see stone entries)

pharmacological.regimen: Thiazides (hypercalciuria), potassium citrate (hypocitraturia/uric acid stones), allopurinol (hyperuricosuria), tiopronin (cystine)

non_pharmacological: Stabilization phase before intervention (typically 12 months); plaque assessment
Penile traction therapy (evidence modest); surgery (plication/grafting) for stable disabling deformity

pharmacological.regimen: Collagenase clostridium histolyticum (Xiaflex) for curvature 30-90 degrees with intact erectile function (IMPRESS trials); interferon alpha-2b intralesional alternative; verapamil intralesional mixed evidence
Oral vitamin E, tamoxifen, colchicine, PDE5i monotherapy (not effective for curvature)

non_pharmacological: Urethral catheterization (suprapubic if urethral fails/contraindicated); record volume; treat precipitant (constipation, drugs, infection)
Trial without catheter after 3-7 days with alpha-blocker started at catheterization

pharmacological.regimen: Alpha-blocker (tamsulosin/alfuzosin) before TWOC doubles success; 5-ARI if enlarged prostate long-term
Clean intermittent self-catheterization or surgery (TURP/HoLEP)

diseases.disease: Neurogenic bladder / neurogenic lower urinary tract dysfunction
non_pharmacological: Urodynamic characterization; protect upper tracts (low-pressure storage)
Clean intermittent catheterization is cornerstone for detrusor underactivity/dyssynergia; manage constipation

pharmacological.regimen: Antimuscarinic (oxybutynin/solifenacin) or mirabegron + CIC; intravesical botulinum toxin A; neuromodulation

Augmentation cystoplasty; urinary diversion

non_pharmacological: Multi-organ assessment (pancreas, salivary, orbits, aorta); biopsy with IgG4+ plasma cells

pharmacological.regimen: Glucocorticoids (prednisone 0.6 mg/kg taper over 3-6 months)
Rituximab highly effective; azathioprine, mycophenolate, methotrexate alternatives
Stents for biliary/ureteral involvement

non_pharmacological: Atherosclerotic RAS: medical therapy is default (ASTRAL/CORAL - stenting rarely beneficial)

See hematology TTP entry (plasma exchange first)

non_pharmacological: Diagnosis after vascular procedure/anticoagulation with livedo, eosinophilia, blue toes

pharmacological.regimen: Statins; steroids/immunosuppression not proven; wound care; dialysis support

pharmacological.regimen: Allopurinol + hydration
Rasburicase (avoid in G6PD deficiency); treat hyperkalemia/hyperphosphatemia aggressively; early RRT for refractory

Plasmapheresis + IVIG +/- rituximab; imlifidase in desensitization settings

Spironolactone first-line; eplerenone if gynecomastia; add amiloride or thiazide as needed; BP and K+ targets

High-dose steroids for mass effect; lifelong replacement usually required

I-131 MIBG therapy (Azedra), PRRT, CVD chemotherapy, targeted therapy; lifelong biochemical surveillance

Lifely monitoring: lipids, bone, metabolic; pituitary surgery/radiation history

pharmacological.regimen: Hydrocortisone replacement as for adrenal insufficiency
Levothyroxine with free T4 (NOT TSH) as target
Testosterone or estrogen-progestin for hypogonadism; gonadotropins (hFSH/hCG) if fertility desired
GH replacement for confirmed deficiency with impaired QoL/metabolic syndrome (monitor IGF-1); contraindicated in active malignancy
Desmopressin for central diabetes insipidus

non_pharmacological: Exclude drug-induced hyperprolactinemia (antipsychotics, metoclopramide), macroprolactin, hypothyroidism, stalk effect
Visual fields for macroadenomas; MRI sella

pharmacological.regimen: Dopamine agonist: cabergoline (0.25-1 mg/week, titrate) preferred over bromocriptine; normalizes prolactin and shrinks tumors in >80-90%
Dose escalation, transsphenoidal surgery, or radiotherapy rare
Bromocriptine or cabergoline for microprolactinoma; stop agonist once pregnant for micro, continue if macro compressive; monitor visual fields

non_pharmacological: IGF-1 screening, OGTT suppression, MRI; screen colon polyps, cardiomyopathy, sleep apnea

pharmacological.regimen: Transsphenoidal surgery by expert pituitary surgeon (cure in microadenomas ~80%)

Somatostatin receptor ligands (octreotide LAR, lanreotide; pasireotide if partial response); GH receptor antagonist pegvisomant (best biochemical control, monitor liver, no tumor imaging effect); dopamine agonist (cabergoline) for mild IGF-1 elevation or mixed GH/PRL
Combination SRL + pegvisomant/cabergoline; radiotherapy/radiosurgery last resort with long latency
Consider for severe pharyngeal edema/cardiac disease to reduce anesthetic risk

non_pharmacological: Water deprivation test / copeptin-based testing (hypertonic saline-stimulated copeptin now preferred)
Central DI: MRI pituitary, screen for germinoma/infiltrative disease; nephrogenic: exclude lithium, hypercalcemia, hypokalemia
