Thiazide + amiloride (amiloride specifically for lithium-induced) + low-solute diet; NSAID (indomethacin) adjunct; stop lithium if possible
Desmopressin (resistant to vasopressinase)

non_pharmacological: Confirm: hyponatremia, low osmolality, urine Osm >100, UNa >30, euvolemic, exclude hypothyroid/adrenal insufficiency
Identify cause: drugs (SSRIs, carbamazepine, PPIs), CNS, pulmonary, malignancy (SCLC); assess severity/symptoms and chronicity - correct Na no faster than 8 mEq/24h to avoid osmotic demyelination

pharmacological.regimen: Hypertonic saline 150 mL 3% over 20 min (repeat x2) targeting +4-6 mEq in first hours
Fluid restriction 800-1000 mL/day first-line; oral salt tabs + loop diuretic; urea powder (15-30 g/day, ESE-recommended)
Vasopressin receptor antagonists (tolvaptan - monitor Na closely, avoid in liver disease, EU caution); demeclocycline rarely; treat underlying cause (e.g., SCLC chemo)
Desmopressin + D5W re-lowering strategy

non_pharmacological: Volume status assessment; stop offending drugs; treat underlying (HF, cirrhosis, nephrotic, adrenal insufficiency, diuretics)

pharmacological.regimen: 0.9% saline cautiously (watch for brisk water diuresis and overcorrection); stop thiazides; glucocorticoids if adrenal
Fluid restriction + loop diuretics; SGLT2i in HF; vaptans selected in HF (not cirrhosis - tolvaptan hepatotoxicity); treat cirrhosis per guidance
Never correct >8 mEq/day; high-risk (alcoholism, malnutrition, hypokalemia) target 4-6

non_pharmacological: Assess volume status; free water deficit = 0.5 x weight x (Na/140 - 1); correct chronic over 48-72 h (<=10 mEq/day)
Treat cause: diarrhea, osmotic diuresis, DI, inadequate access to water

pharmacological.regimen: Restore circulation with isotonic saline FIRST, then correct deficit with D5W or hypotonic fluids
Desmopressin if central; fluids + thiazide/amiloride if nephrogenic
D5W + loop diuretic; dialysis if renal failure

non_pharmacological: ECG monitoring for significant abnormalities; identify renal vs GI losses (urine K), drugs (diuretics, ACEi, spironolactone, TMP)
Correct magnesium (refractory hypokalemia); avoid dextrose-containing fluids in hypokalemia

pharmacological.regimen: Oral KCl 40-80 mEq/day divided (first-line); IV KCl 10-20 mEq/h with ECG if severe (<2.5 or arrhythmia); treat cause; K-sparing diuretics for chronic diuretic-induced losses
IV calcium gluconate/chloride if ECG changes; insulin 10 units + 25 g dextrose; nebulized salbutamol 10-20 mg; sodium bicarbonate if acidotic; dialysis for refractory
Diet review, stop K-raising drugs, diuretics; potassium binders: patiromer or sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (enable RAASi continuation in CKD/HF); sodium polystyrene acutely only

non_pharmacological: Risk stratification (ASCVD risk; targets: very high risk LDL <1.4 mmol/L [55 mg/dL] and >=50% reduction; ESC 2024 suggests lower in extreme risk)
Mediterranean diet, exercise, weight loss, smoking cessation; exclude secondary causes (hypothyroid, nephrotic, liver, drugs)
FH: cascade genetic screening of relatives (Dutch Lipid Clinic/Simon Broome criteria)

pharmacological.regimen: High-intensity statin (atorvastatin 40-80, rosuvastatin 20-40)
Add ezetimibe 10 mg
PCSK9 inhibitor (evolocumab, alirocumab) or inclisiran (siRNA, twice-yearly dosing) for very high risk/FH not at goal
Rechallenge with different statin/lower dose; bempedoic acid; inclisiran
Treat secondary causes; icosapent ethyl (EPA 2 g BID) in high-risk with TG 1.5-5.6 on statin (REDUCE-IT); fibrate for TG >10 mmol/L (pancreatitis prevention)
Measure once; aggressive LDL lowering; pelacarsen/olpasiran antisense agents in trials; PCSK9i lower Lp(a) ~25%
Lomitapide, evinacumab, LDL apheresis

non_pharmacological: Weight loss 5-10%; 150-300 min/week moderate activity; Mediterranean/DASH diet; sleep optimization

pharmacological.regimen: Per individual components: statins, antihypertensives (ACEi/ARB), SGLT2i/GLP-1 RA for T2D/obesity; no single drug for the syndrome
See obesity entry

non_pharmacological: Structured lifestyle intervention: 500-750 kcal/day deficit, high-protein/Mediterranean patterns, 150-300 min/week activity, behavioral strategies (self-monitoring, sleep, stress)
Bariatric/metabolic surgery: BMI >=35 (or >=30 with comorbid T2D/metabolic disease); sleeve gastrectomy, Roux-en-Y, duodenal switch; improves mortality and comorbidities

pharmacological.regimen: Incretin-based: tirzepatide (SURMOUNT-1, up to ~22.5% weight loss) or semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly (STEP trials ~15%); liraglutide 3 mg daily
Phentermine/topiramate ER, naltrexone/bupropion, orlistat (modest efficacy); phentermine short-term
T2D: tirzepatide/semaglutide; HFpEF: semaglutide (STEP-HFpEF); OSA: tirzepatide (SURMOUNT-OSA 2024); CKD: semaglutide (FLOW renal benefit)
Obesity is chronic - continue effective therapy; weight regain expected after discontinuation

non_pharmacological: Lifestyle first-line for all: 5-10% weight loss improves ovulation and metabolic profile
Screen metabolic syndrome, OSA, NAFLD, depression; endometrial protection if oligomenorrheic

pharmacological.regimen: Combined oral contraceptive first-line (ethinylestradiol + low-androgenicity progestin); add spironolactone (or finasteride/flutamide where used) for hirsutism after 6 months with reliable contraception
Metformin for T2D/IGT or metabolic risk; GLP-1 RA for obesity

Letrozole first-line ovulation induction (PPCOS II); clomiphene alternative +/- metformin; gonadotropins or laparoscopic ovarian drilling second-line; IVF third-line; inositol adjunct evidence emerging
Eflornithine topical, cosmetic methods, laser

non_pharmacological: CBT for vasomotor symptoms; cooling strategies; vaginal moisturizers/lubricants; pelvic floor exercises; bone/cardiovascular risk management

pharmacological.line: First-line (moderate-severe VMS, <60 y or within 10 y of menopause)
pharmacological.regimen: Menopausal hormone therapy: estrogen (+ progestogen if uterus intact; micronized progesterone preferred) - transdermal estradiol preferred if VTE/metabolic risk
Fezolinetant (neurokinin 3 receptor antagonist, FDA 2023), SSRIs/SNRIs (venlafaxine, paroxetine), gabapentin, clonidine, oxybutynin
Low-dose vaginal estrogen (cream/tablet/ring), vaginal DHEA (prasterone), or ospemifene
MHT helps bone; bisphosphonates/denosumab if osteoporosis

non_pharmacological: Confirm low testosterone on 2 morning samples + LH/FSH (primary vs secondary); exclude prolactinoma, opioids, obesity
Discuss fertility (testosterone suppresses spermatogenesis); baseline Hct, PSA in at-risk

pharmacological.regimen: Gel daily, IM cypionate/enanthate q1-2wk or undecanoate q10-14wk; monitor Hct (hold if >54%), symptoms, PSA; avoid in prostate/breast cancer, recent MI/stroke, severe OSA, uncontrolled HF, fertility plans
hCG +/- FSH for secondary hypogonadism; clomiphene off-label alternative
Address opioid use first

non_pharmacological: Safe sun exposure; dietary sources (fatty fish, fortified foods); screen at-risk (obesity, malabsorption, dark skin, institutionalized, renal/hepatic disease)

pharmacological.regimen: Cholecalciferol 50,000 IU weekly x6-8 weeks (or 6000 IU daily) then maintenance 800-2000 IU/day; aim 25(OH)D >=50 nmol/L (IOM) - some societies 75
Higher-dose vitamin D + calcium; treat cause (malabsorption: higher doses or calcifediol)
Active analogs (alfacalcidol/calcitriol) if 1-alpha hydroxylation impaired

diseases.key_guideline: Endocrine Society 2024 Vitamin D Guideline (conditional supplementation in high-risk groups)

non_pharmacological: Identify cause: pernicious anemia (intrinsic factor Ab), atrophic gastritis, metformin/PPI use, vegan diet, malabsorption, alcohol
Check B12 before folate therapy (folate can worsen neurologic B12 deficiency)

pharmacological.regimen: IM hydroxocobalamin 1 mg 3x/week x2 weeks then 3-monthly (pernicious anemia lifelong); high-dose oral (1000-2000 mcg/day) effective for dietary/absorption issues; monitor K+ during repletion
Folic acid 1-5 mg/day x4 months + treat cause; prophylaxis 400 mcg preconception (5 mg if prior NTD)
Reticulocyte response, CBC, neurological recovery

non_pharmacological: Common causes: PPIs, diuretics, alcohol, diarrhea, aminoglycosides, cisplatin; often accompanies refractory hypoK/hypoCa

pharmacological.regimen: IV magnesium sulfate for severe/symptomatic (torsades risk); oral magnesium salts for chronic mild; replete K+ and Ca2+ concurrently
Stop Mg sources; IV calcium for cardiac toxicity; saline + loop diuretic; dialysis if severe

non_pharmacological: Risk-stratify malnourished patients before feeding (NICE criteria); start low (10 kcal/kg) and advance slowly; daily electrolytes days 1-7
Severe (<0.3 mmol/L) or symptomatic (weakness, hemolysis, respiratory failure): IV replacement

pharmacological.regimen: IV sodium/potassium phosphate; thiamine 200-300 mg BEFORE feeding in at-risk; replete K+ and Mg2+
Phosphate + calcitriol; burosumab (anti-FGF23) for X-linked hypophosphatemia and tumor-induced osteomalacia

non_pharmacological: Avoid porphyrinogenic drugs (safe list: porphyria drug databases); avoid fasting/alcohol; treat intercurrent illness
Diagnose with urine PBG/ALA during attack; genetic counseling

pharmacological.regimen: IV hemin (3-4 mg/kg x4 days) as soon as possible; IV glucose loading for mild; opioids/ondansetron for pain/nausea (safe); correct hyponatremia
Givosiran (siRNA targeting ALAS1) monthly SC; GnRH analogs for cyclical attacks
Phlebotomy or low-dose hydroxychloroquine; treat HCV/iron/alcohol triggers

non_pharmacological: Risk-adapted: lobectomy for low-risk unifocal; total thyroidectomy +/- RAI for higher risk; RAI remnant ablation per ATA risk

pharmacological.regimen: Levothyroxine to TSH target per risk (<0.1 high risk; 0.1-0.5 intermediate; low-normal low risk)

Sorafenib or lenvatinib first-line (SELECT/DECISION); dabrafenib+trametinib for BRAF V600E; NTRK inhibitors for NTRK fusions; re-challenge RAI with redifferentiation agents (dabrafenib/selumetinib) in trials
Surgery; vandetanib/cabozantinib for advanced; selpercatinib/pralsetinib for RET-mutant; thyroid cancer anaplastic: dabrafenib+trametinib if BRAF+, immunotherapy trials

non_pharmacological: Alcohol abstinence; very-low-fat diet (<10-15% calories) until TG <500; glycemic control; stop estrogen/OCP, retinoids, tamoxifen if contributors

pharmacological.regimen: Fibrate (fenofibrate) + omega-3 fatty acids (4 g/day EPA/DHA or icosapent ethyl); insulin infusion acutely if hyperglycemic (activates LPL)
Insulin-dextrose infusion; plasmapheresis in select severe cases; NPO, standard pancreatitis care

non_pharmacological: Review drugs: antipsychotics (risperidone highest), metoclopramide, domperidone, verapamil, opioids
Exclude pregnancy, hypothyroidism, renal failure, macroprolactin

pharmacological.regimen: Stop/switch culprit if possible (psychiatry input; switch to aripiprazole/quetiapine where feasible); dopamine agonist if symptomatic and drug cannot be stopped; treat underlying cause

diseases.disease: Growth hormone deficiency / short stature (pediatric endocrine)
non_pharmacological: Auxology tracking (height velocity); bone age; screen chronic disease, celiac, hypothyroid, Turner syndrome
Psychosocial support; treat underlying systemic disease

pharmacological.regimen: Recombinant GH daily; monitor IGF-1, glucose, scoliosis, slipped epiphysis
Turner syndrome, SGA without catch-up, Prader-Willi, chronic renal insufficiency, SHOX deficiency, idiopathic short stature (selected)
Reassurance; short course low-dose testosterone/estrogen for psychological distress

non_pharmacological: Beta-thalassemia major: regular transfusion program (target pre-transfusion Hb 9-10.5), ferritin monitoring, cardiac/liver MRI T2*
Folic acid; avoid iron supplementation; splenectomy only selected (vaccinate); HSCT curative (matched sibling)

pharmacological.regimen: Deferasirox (oral, first-line), deferoxamine (SC), deferiprone (neutropenia monitoring); combination for cardiac iron
Luspatercept (BELIEVE trial) for transfusion burden; HSCT; gene therapy: betibeglogene autotemcel (Zynteglo) approved for TDT
Supportive; folate; transfusion as needed

diseases.disease: Diabetes and pregnancy / preconception care in T1D
non_pharmacological: High-dose folic acid 5 mg; optimize HbA1c <6.5% preconception; CGM recommended in pregnancy
Retinopathy screening preconception and each trimester

Post-bariatric hypoglycemia: small low-GI meals, protein/fiber, avoid simple carbs

pharmacological.regimen: Surgical enucleation/resection definitive; diazoxide + thiazide to control hypoglycemia preoperatively; everolimus for malignant
Acarbose first; octreotide or diazoxide if refractory; pasireotide trials; rarely reversal/revision

non_pharmacological: Monitor PTH, Ca, PO4 per CKD stage; dietary phosphate restriction

Manage components per guidelines; somatostatin analogs for pancreatic NETs
Belzutifan (HIF-2alpha inhibitor) approved 2021 for VHL-associated RCC/CNS hemangioblastomas/panNET not requiring immediate surgery

non_pharmacological: Debulking/metastatic liver-directed therapies; avoid triggers (alcohol, catecholamines) pre-procedure to prevent crisis

pharmacological.regimen: Somatostatin analogs (octreotide LAR or lanreotide) for symptoms and antiproliferative effect (PROMID/CLARINET)
Telotristat ethyl (tryptophan hydroxylase inhibitor)
PRRT (Lu-177-DOTATATE), everolimus, liver-directed therapy; carcinoid crisis: IV octreotide bolus/infusion

non_pharmacological: As per acute porphyrias; prophylactic hemin for very frequent attacks replaced by givosiran

pharmacological.regimen: Duloxetine, pregabalin/gabapentin, or amitriptyline/nortriptyline
Combine mechanisms (e.g., duloxetine + pregabalin); topical capsaicin 8% patch or lidocaine for focal
Chronic opioids; disease-modifying: aldose reductase inhibitors not widely approved
Orthostatic hypotension: fluids/salt, midodrine, droxidopa; gastroparesis and ED per entries

pharmacological.regimen: Treat the cause; iron replacement if absolute or functional deficiency

Transfusion support; ESA in select low-risk MDS; luspatercept for MDS with ring sideroblasts

Rituximab (now often preferred before splenectomy per first-line RCT data); splenectomy alternative
Immunosuppressants (azathioprine, MMF, cyclosporine), fostamatinib trials, daratumumab case series
Avoid cold; rituximab monotherapy or bendamustine-rituximab; sutimlimab (C1s inhibitor) approved for hemolysis control

non_pharmacological: Flow cytometry (FLAER); screen for hemolysis, thrombosis, marrow failure; folic acid

Meningococcal vaccination + prophylaxis with complement blockers; anticoagulation if thrombosis (with complement blockade)
HSCT for severe aplastic overlap or complement-inhibitor failure

Genetic counseling; neonatal jaundice surveillance

pharmacological.regimen: Supportive: stop trigger, treat infection, transfuse if severe; folic acid
G6PD testing before radical P. vivax cure (see malaria entry)

non_pharmacological: Penicillin prophylaxis from 2 months + pneumococcal/meningococcal/Hib/influenza vaccination
Transcranial Doppler screening in children; chronic transfusion for abnormal TCD or recurrent stroke
Pain plan, hydration, avoid triggers (cold, dehydration, altitude); hydroxyurea counseling; multidisciplinary care

Broad-spectrum antibiotics (cephalosporin + macrolide), oxygen, bronchodilators if reactive airway, simple or exchange transfusion, pain control

diseases.key_guideline: ASH 2020 SCD Guidelines; NHLBI 2014; FDA gene therapy approvals 2023

Splenectomy for moderate-severe disease (delay until age >=6; vaccinate pre-splenectomy: pneumococcal, meningococcal ACWY+B, Hib; lifelong infection vigilance)

non_pharmacological: Exclude inherited marrow failure (Fanconi, telomere disorders), PNH clone, MDS, hepatitis, drugs/toxins
Transfuse CMV-negative, irradiated, leukoreduced products; avoid family donors before transplant

pharmacological.line: Young (<=40) with matched sibling donor, severe disease
pharmacological.regimen: HSCT first-line
Immunosuppression: horse ATG x4 days + cyclosporine (12+ months) + eltrombopag (triple therapy, RACE trial) - horse ATG superior to rabbit ATG
Matched unrelated donor HSCT; second IST cycle; eltrombopag; androgens (danazol) in telomeropathies

non_pharmacological: IPSS-M risk stratification; mutation panel; exclude reversible cytopenias
Supportive: transfusion support, iron chelation in long-term transfused

Hypomethylating agents: azacitidine (OS benefit, Fenaux) or decitabine; HSCT only curative option for fit patients
Azacitidine + venetoclax or magrolimab trials; imetelstat approved 2024 (US) for lower-risk MDS transfusion-dependent anemia after ESA
Clinical trials preferred; decitabine 10-day schedules studied

TLS prophylaxis, antimicrobial prophylaxis in neutropenia, transfusion support; CNS prophylaxis not routine

Venetoclax + azacitidine/decitabine (VIALE-A) or low-dose cytarabine + venetoclax
ATRA + arsenic trioxide for low/intermediate risk (cure >90%); add anthracycline/gemtuzumab for high risk; manage DIC aggressively
HiDAC cycles for favorable risk; allogeneic HSCT for intermediate/adverse risk in CR1
FLT3 inhibitors (gilteritinib); IDH1/2 inhibitors (ivosidenib, enasidenib); venetoclax combinations; HSCT; menin inhibitors (revumenib approved 2024 for KMT2A-rearranged R/R AML)

non_pharmacological: Risk stratify by age, WBC, genetics (BCR-ABL1, KMT2A, Ph-like, iAMP21), MRD
CNS prophylaxis (intrathecal MTX/cytarabine) essential; TLS precautions

pharmacological.regimen: Multi-agent chemotherapy (induction/consolidation/maintenance with asparaginase, vincristine, steroids, MTX); BFM-style backbones
Add TKI (dasatinib/imatinib) to chemotherapy; steroid-sparing dasatinib + blinatumomab regimens (GIMEMA D-ALBA)
Blinatumomab (BiTE), inotuzumab ozogamicin (anti-CD22), then allo-HSCT; CD19 CAR-T (tisagenlecleucel) for pediatric/young adult R/R B-ALL
Intensive chemo; nelarabine added for T-LBL/ALL (COG data); HSCT in high risk
Pediatric-inspired regimens; ponatinib for T315I; maintenance

diseases.key_guideline: NCCN ALL; GRAALL; pediatric COG protocols

non_pharmacological: BCR-ABL1 quantification by PCR at baseline, 3, 6, 12 months; ELN milestones (<=10% at 3 months)
Cardiovascular risk optimization (ponatinib/nilotinib vascular risk)

pharmacological.regimen: Imatinib 400 mg, dasatinib 100 mg, nilotinib 300 mg BID, or bosutinib 400 mg; choice by comorbidities/age/goals
Switch TKI guided by ABL kinase domain mutations (T315I: ponatinib or asciminib); asciminib (STAMP inhibitor) approved for >=2 prior TKIs and first-line (ASCEMBL/ASC4FIRST)
Attempt after deep molecular response (MR4.5) >=2 years with close PCR monitoring; restart TKI if loss of MMR
AML/ALL-type induction + TKI, then allo-HSCT

non_pharmacological: Stage (Rai/Binet); treat only symptomatic/progressive disease - NOT lymphocytosis alone
Test IGHV mutation, del17p/TP53, del11q/13q before therapy; infection prophylaxis awareness

Treat as DLBCL (R-CHOP-like -> clinical trials/CAR-T)
IVIG for recurrent infections with hypogammaglobulinemia; VZV prophylaxis with venetoclax regimens per local policy

non_pharmacological: Low-dose aspirin for all (no contraindication); phlebotomy to hematocrit <45% (CYTO-PV)
Manage cardiovascular risk factors; pruritus care

pharmacological.regimen: Hydroxyurea first-line cytoreduction; pegylated interferon alfa-2a (especially younger/pregnancy-planning; ropeginterferon approved)
Ruxolitinib (JAK1/2 inhibitor, RESPONSE trial); busulfan in elderly selected
SSRIs/antihistamines for aquagenic pruritus; iron deficiency NOT treated routinely (fuels erythrocytosis)
Per MF guidelines; transplant consideration

non_pharmacological: Risk stratify (age >60, JAK2+, prior thrombosis); exclude reactive thrombocytosis, CML, MDS
Aspirin in microvascular symptoms; once/twice daily in extreme thrombocytosis with acquired vWD caution

pharmacological.regimen: Hydroxyurea first-line; peg-IFN alfa-2a for younger/pregnancy; anagrelide second-line (PT-1 non-inferior but more MF transformation and arterial events)
Check vWF before aspirin; plateletpheresis in emergencies
Aspirin + LMWH if high-risk; IFN for cytoreduction

non_pharmacological: DIPSS/MIPSS70 risk stratification; JAK2/CALR/MPL testing; transfusion support
Allogeneic HSCT is only curative therapy for intermediate-2/high risk fit patients

pharmacological.regimen: Ruxolitinib first-line (COMFORT trials); fedratinib after ruxolitinib
Momelotinib (MOMENTUM; approved 2023, improves anemia via ACVR1); pacritinib if platelets <50 (PERSIST trials); danazol, ESA, luspatercept adjuncts
Transfusions, androgens, splenic irradiation rarely

non_pharmacological: Exclude secondary causes (HIV, HCV, lupus, CLL, drugs, H. pylori in some populations)
Treat only significant bleeding or platelets <20-30 with bleeding risk - not numbers alone; avoid NSAIDs/antiplatelets

pharmacological.regimen: Corticosteroids: dexamethasone 40 mg x4 days cycles OR prednisone 0.5-1 mg/kg short course (taper off by 6-8 weeks); add IVIG or anti-D if rapid rise needed (bleeding, pre-surgery)

TPO receptor agonists (eltrombopag, romiplostim, avatrombopag) - often preferred over splenectomy now; rituximab; fostamatinib (SYK inhibitor); splenectomy (durable in ~60%, delay >12 months if possible)

pharmacological.regimen: Clomipramine low dose or SSRI (case series); improve sleep continuity; avoid stimulants

diseases.disease: Fatal familial insomnia / prion-related sleep disorders
non_pharmacological: PRNP mutation; progressive insomnia, dysautonomia, dementia; genetic counseling for family; supportive/palliative care

pharmacological.regimen: No effective treatment; sedatives generally ineffective; symptom-directed comfort care; clinical trials (antisense) ongoing

non_pharmacological: Consistent bedtime routines, visual schedules, graduated extinction/parental presence strategies for behavioral insomnia of childhood
ASD: higher insomnia prevalence; screen for OSA/RLS; structured sleep hygiene programs first

pharmacological.regimen: Behavioral interventions first; short-term melatonin 1-5 mg if sleep-onset insomnia persists
Behavioral therapy + melatonin (including prolonged-release 2-10 mg; evidence strong); avoid chronic sedating antihistamines/antipsychotics for sleep
Optimize stimulant timing/dose; melatonin effective for delayed sleep onset in ADHD

diseases.key_guideline: AASM pediatric insomnia; AAP ASD sleep; ESRS pediatric

non_pharmacological: Screen with Rockwood Clinical Frailty Scale or Fried phenotype in adults >=65; comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA) improves outcomes in hospital
Resistance + balance exercise programs (multicomponent training is the most effective intervention); protein intake 1.0-1.2 g/kg/day; vitamin D if deficient
Prehabilitation before elective surgery; deprescribing harmful medications; social prescribing

pharmacological.regimen: Treat contributors: anemia, hypothyroidism, depression, heart failure, sarcopenia; avoid sedatives/anticholinergics; vitamin D supplementation only if deficient (no benefit in replete)
No approved drug; senolytics, myostatin inhibitors in trials

diseases.key_guideline: BGS Fit for Frailty; NICE Older People; EUGMS

non_pharmacological: Annual falls risk screen >=65 (ask about falls in past 12 months); multifactorial intervention if >=1 fall
Strength and balance training (Otago, Tai Chi) - strongest evidence; home hazard assessment; vision correction; footwear review; vitamin D/calcium only if deficient/institutionalized
Post-fall: lying-down plan, telecare/alarm; syncope workup if collapse without trip

pharmacological.regimen: Deprescribe/taper: benzodiazepines/Z-drugs, sedating antihistamines, anticholinergics, polypharmacy >=5, vasodilators in postural hypotension; review antihypertensives if postural drop
Non-pharm first (slow position change, compression, hydration, small meals); midodrine or fludrocortisone if persistent symptomatic; droxidopa (US) for neurogenic OH
Assess fracture risk per osteoporosis entry after injurious falls

diseases.key_guideline: NICE Falls 2013 (2023 watch); AGS/BGS Falls Guideline 2011 + updates

diseases.disease: Delirium prevention and management (see psychiatry) - geriatric protocol
non_pharmacological: 4AT rapid screening in hospital; multi-component prevention bundles (HELP, PINCER): orientation, mobilization, sleep, hydration, vision/hearing aids, pain control
Treat precipitants: infection, urinary retention, constipation, hypoxia, metabolic, drugs

pharmacological.regimen: No drug prevents or treats delirium; low-dose haloperidol/olanzapine ONLY for dangerous agitation; avoid benzodiazepines except alcohol withdrawal; melatonin prophylaxis evidence weak
Avoid meperidine and long-acting benzodiazepines; regional anesthesia where possible; postoperative sleep protocol

diseases.key_guideline: NICE Delirium 2023; AGS Beers 2023; SCCM PADIS

non_pharmacological: Structured medication review (>=5 medicines = polypharmacy; >=10 = excessive); STOPP/START and Beers criteria screening
Patient goals of care first; prioritize deprescribing: PPI without indication, long-term benzodiazepine, chronic NSAID, sulfonylurea in elderly, duplicate therapy

pharmacological.regimen: One change at a time, slow taper for dependent classes (benzodiazepines, opioids, antidepressants); monitor withdrawal; document indication for every continued medicine

Benzodiazepines: diazepam taper over months; PPI: rebound acid - taper over 4-8 weeks; anticholinergics: switch to lower-burden alternatives; tight glycemic control relaxation in limited life expectancy (HbA1c 7.5-8%)
Review all renally cleared drugs at eGFR changes (DOACs, metformin, digoxin, gabapentinoids)

diseases.key_guideline: NICE Medicines in Older People (in progress); AGS Beers 2023; STOPP-START v3 2023

diseases.disease: Urinary incontinence in older adults (see urology/OBGYN) - geriatric approach
non_pharmacological: Assess transient causes (DIAPPERS mnemonic: delirium, infection, atrophic vaginitis, meds, polyuria, excess output, restricted mobility, stool impaction)
Containment products, toileting schedules, prompted voiding in dependent patients; pelvic floor training for capable patients

pharmacological.regimen: OAB: mirabegron preferred in elderly (fewer cognitive effects than oxybutynin - avoid oxybutynin in cognitive impairment); stress: duloxetine/surgery; overflow: treat retention (alpha-blocker, catheterize)
Indwelling catheters for incontinence alone (infection, delirium); antimuscarinics with high anticholinergic burden in dementia

non_pharmacological: EWGSOP2 criteria: low strength + low mass/quality; grip strength screening
Progressive resistance training 2-3x/week core intervention; protein 1.0-1.5 g/kg/day spread across meals; leucine-rich sources; vitamin D if deficient

pharmacological.regimen: Treat underlying causes (hypogonadism, HF, COPD, cancer, malabsorption); protein/vitamin D supplementation if deficient; anabolic agents (testosterone in confirmed hypogonadism only)
Myostatin inhibitors, ghrelin agonists, selective androgen receptor modulators in trials

diseases.disease: Dysphagia in older adults / aspiration prevention
non_pharmacological: Bedside swallow screen post-stroke; videofluoroscopy/FEES for persistent symptoms; dietitian texture modification (IDDSI framework)
Oral hygiene programs reduce aspiration pneumonia; upright positioning during/after meals; chin-tuck strategies per SLP; PEG for prolonged inability when consistent with goals

pharmacological.regimen: Treat stroke/Parkinson/dementia causes; optimize Parkinson meds timing with meals; ACE inhibitor may reduce aspiration in some stroke populations (weak evidence); no drug improves swallowing per se
Antibiotics per pneumonia entry; focus on prevention over repeated courses

diseases.key_guideline: NICE swallowing difficulties; RCP stroke national guidelines

diseases.disease: Parkinson disease in the elderly (see neurology) - geriatric nuances
non_pharmacological: As neurology entry; fall prevention, dementia screening, hallucination management, orthostatic hypotension care

pharmacological.regimen: Levodopa preferred over agonists in elderly (less psychosis/orthostasis); avoid anticholinergics entirely; cholinesterase inhibitors for PDD; pimavanserin for PD psychosis (US)
Avoid metoclopramide/prochlorperazine/haloperidol (dopamine blockade); domperidone preferred for nausea where available

diseases.disease: Hypertension in the very old (see cardiovascular) - geriatric targets
non_pharmacological: As cardiovascular entry; individualize targets in frailty (SBP <130 tolerated fit, <140-150 frail); standing BP check in all treated elderly
Monotherapy initiation in >80 or frail; slow uptitration

pharmacological.regimen: Thiazide-like or CCB or ACEi/ARB single agent start; relax targets if postural symptoms, recurrent falls, or limited life expectancy; deprescribe if SBP consistently <120 with symptoms
Alpha-blockers and centrally acting agents as first-line; aggressive combination in frail oldest-old

diseases.key_guideline: ESC 2024 HTN (frailty section); SPRINT-SENIOR; HYVET legacy

diseases.disease: Atrial fibrillation in the elderly (see cardiovascular) - anticoagulation decisions
non_pharmacological: CHA2DS2-VA score drives anticoagulation regardless of age; frailty/falls alone rarely justify withholding (stroke harm > bleed harm usually)
DOAC dose adjustment by age/renal function/weight; renal function review q6-12 months

pharmacological.regimen: DOAC first-line; apixaban favored in renal impairment/elderly; avoid aspirin for stroke prevention in AF (ineffective, bleeds); LAAO if anticoagulation contraindicated
Reassess only with limited life expectancy or recurrent serious bleeding; fall risk alone not an indication to stop

diseases.disease: Diabetes in older adults (see endocrine) - relaxed targets
non_pharmacological: Individualized HbA1c: 7-7.5% fit, 8-8.5% frail/multimorbid; avoid hypoglycemia above all (fall/cognitive risk)
Deintensification: stop sulfonylureas, relax insulin regimens, simplify

pharmacological.regimen: Reduce/stop insulin in type 2 if hypoglycemia or limited benefit; DPP-4 inhibitors well tolerated in elderly; avoid glyburide/glibenclamide entirely; SGLT2i with dehydration caution; metformin to eGFR 30
CGM for insulin-treated frail; glucagon education for carers; relax targets after any severe episode

diseases.key_guideline: ADA Older Adults Standards 2025; Endocrine Society diabetes in older adults

diseases.disease: Cancer treatment decisions in older adults
non_pharmacological: Geriatric assessment (GA) predicts toxicity better than ECOG alone; CGA-guided management reduces grade 3-5 toxicity (GAP70+ trial)
Goals of care discussion; dose adjustments by organ function; support systems for adherence/oral agents

pharmacological.regimen: Per oncology entries with geriatric dose modification; screening tools (G8, VES-13); SIOG/ASCO geriatric oncology guidance; avoid undertreatment solely by age
G-CSF prophylaxis at lower FN thresholds; bone protection with aromatase inhibitors/ADT; palliative care early integration

diseases.key_guideline: SIOG guidelines; ASCO Older Adults with Cancer 2023

non_pharmacological: Advance care planning; prognosis communication (surprise question); goals-concordant care; family/carer support; spiritual care
Anticipatory prescribing for terminal symptoms; syringe driver for continuous symptom control

pharmacological.regimen: WHO analgesic ladder; opioids titrated (morphine/oxycodone; fentanyl/buprenorphine patches if renal impairment); breakthrough dose 1/6 of 24-h total; laxatives + antiemetic with opioids; corticosteroids for bone/capsular pain
Opioids (oral/nebulized/SC) + fan/positioning; oxygen only if hypoxemic; anxiolytics for distress
Repositioning; hyoscine butylbromide/glycopyrronium (antimuscarinic); suctioning rarely helpful
Treat reversible causes (urinary retention, pain) first; midazolam/haloperidol; palliative sedation protocol for refractory suffering
Haloperidol, levomepromazine, metoclopramide (avoid in complete bowel obstruction), cyclizine

diseases.key_guideline: NICE Care of Dying Adults 2017; ESMO Palliative; WHO palliative care

non_pharmacological: Screen at-risk presentations (unexplained injuries, poor hygiene, medication non-adherence, caregiver conflict); capacity assessment
Multi-agency safeguarding referral; social services involvement; safety planning

pharmacological.regimen: Treat injuries; document findings meticulously; carer support/respite reduces neglect risk; no pharmacologic intervention for the condition itself

diseases.key_guideline: WHO elder abuse; NICE safeguarding adults

non_pharmacological: Complete decongestive therapy (CDT): manual lymphatic drainage + compression bandaging/garments + skin care + exercise (cornerstone)
Weight loss; meticulous skin care preventing cellulitis (recurrent episodes worsen lymphedema); avoid venipuncture/BP on affected limb in secondary lymphedema
Supermicrosurgery (lymphovenous anastomosis) or vascularized lymph node transfer in selected early cases; liposuction for end-stage non-pitting volume

pharmacological.regimen: Penicillin V prophylaxis after >=2 cellulitis episodes (or benzathine penicillin IM); treat episodes promptly
Diuretics (ineffective, worsen protein deposition); benzopyrones (coumarin hepatotoxicity)
Treat malignancy/filariasis/venous disease; compression garments lifelong after successful decongestion

non_pharmacological: Duplex ultrasound to map extent (rule out DVT extension at saphenofemoral junction)
Compression, elevation, NSAIDs for short segments <5 cm away from junction

pharmacological.line: Extensive SVT (>=5 cm) or near deep junction
pharmacological.regimen: Fondaparinux 2.5 mg daily x45 days (CALISTO trial) first-line; rivaroxaban 10 mg x45 days alternative (SURPRISE); LMWH prophylactic dose alternative
Treat as DVT (full anticoagulation) or urgent surgical ligation
NSAIDs/topical treatments for symptoms; exclude underlying malignancy in recurrent migratory SVT (Trousseau)

non_pharmacological: Diagnosis often delayed - 'pain out of proportion to exam' + AF/vascular history = CTA urgently
Immediate surgical/vascular team; resuscitation; bowel viability assessment (second-look laparotomy)

pharmacological.regimen: Systemic anticoagulation (UFH) at diagnosis; broad-spectrum antibiotics; aggressive fluids
Open embolectomy or endovascular aspiration/thrombolysis per expertise
Endovascular stenting or bypass; revascularize before resecting where possible
Stop vasoconstrictors, optimize perfusion, intra-arterial vasodilators (papaverine) in select; venous thrombosis: anticoagulation alone

diseases.key_guideline: ESVS mesenteric 2024; WSES acute mesenteric ischemia

non_pharmacological: Postprandial pain, weight loss, food fear; CTA shows >=2 vessel stenosis typically
Nutritional support; revascularization for symptomatic disease (endovascular first-line, open for durability in fit)

pharmacological.regimen: Antiplatelet + high-intensity statin + smoking cessation (atherosclerotic disease); small frequent meals; treat malnutrition
Antiplatelet therapy; surveillance imaging; monitor for median arcuate ligament syndrome mimics in young

non_pharmacological: Neurogenic TOS (95%): physiotherapy first-line (scalene/postural strengthening, 3-6 months); avoid prolonged overhead positions
Venous TOS (effort thrombosis, Paget-Schroetter): urgent anticoagulation + catheter-directed thrombolysis followed by first-rib decompression
Arterial TOS (rare, structural anomaly): surgical repair

pharmacological.regimen: Physiotherapy +/- neuropathic analgesics; botulinum toxin to scalenes selected; surgical decompression (first rib/scalenectomy) only after failed conservative with clear compression
Anticoagulation 3-6 months after thrombolysis/surgery; thrombolysis ideally within 14 days of symptom onset
Anticoagulation alone without decompression in young effort thrombosis (high recurrence)

diseases.key_guideline: SVS reporting standards TOS; RVD consensus

non_pharmacological: Left iliofemoral DVT predominance in young women; CTV/IVUS for diagnosis
Catheter-directed thrombolysis + iliac vein stenting for acute iliofemoral DVT with severe symptoms (ATTRACT trial nuance: no overall PTS reduction but reduces moderate-severe PTS and symptoms)

pharmacological.regimen: Standard VTE anticoagulation per cardiovascular entry; post-stent antiplatelet + anticoagulation course per center
Pharmacomechanical thrombectomy; compression stockings for residual symptoms

diseases.key_guideline: AVF/SIR iliofemoral DVT guidance; ATTRACT interpretation

non_pharmacological: Prevention: effective early anticoagulation; weight loss, exercise, elevation

Graduated compression stockings for symptom relief (SOX trial negative for prevention but helpful for established symptoms); wound care for venous ulceration; stenting for residual iliac obstruction in select

pharmacological.regimen: Compression therapy; venoactive agents (MPFF) modest benefit for symptoms; pentoxifylline + compression for venous ulcers; treat ulceration per wound entry
Venous angioplasty/stenting for symptomatic chronic iliofemoral obstruction in expert centers

diseases.disease: Raynaud phenomenon secondary / digital ischemia (see rheumatology) - vascular management
non_pharmacological: As rheumatology entry; nailfold capillaroscopy, ANA to stratify; avoid cold exposure and vasoconstrictors

pharmacological.regimen: CCB first; PDE5i, IV prostacyclin for critical digital ischemia; bosentan prevents new digital ulcers in SSc; sympathectomy last resort

diseases.disease: Aortic aneurysm surveillance programs (see cardiovascular) - vascular medicine coordination
non_pharmacological: As cardiovascular AAA entry; thoracic aortic surveillance by CTA/MRI for bicuspid/Marfan/connective tissue
Smoking cessation slows AAA growth (strongest modifiable factor); family screening in early-onset TAA

pharmacological.regimen: Statin + antiplatelet + BP control; no drug shrinks aneurysms; repair thresholds per cardiovascular entry; beta-blocker in Marfan/Loeys-Dietz

non_pharmacological: FMD: string-of-beads on CTA; screen for aneurysm/dissection elsewhere; antiplatelet therapy
Renal artery aneurysm: repair at >=3 cm, women planning pregnancy, or enlarging

pharmacological.regimen: Aspirin daily; angioplasty for hypertension from renal FMD (not stented); carotid/cerebral FMD: antiplatelet, avoid neck manipulation; aneurysm surveillance
BP control; endovascular coiling/stent-graft or open repair per anatomy

diseases.disease: Vasculitis of large/medium vessels - vascular medicine overlap (see rheumatology)
non_pharmacological: As rheumatology entries (GCA, Takayasu, PAN); imaging surveillance for aneurysm/stenosis; graft patency monitoring

pharmacological.regimen: Steroid-based induction + tocilizumab/immunosuppressants; revascularization in quiescent phase only; antiplatelet individualized

non_pharmacological: Pernio: cold avoidance, keep core warm, loose footwear; exclude chilblain lupus/perniosis in atypical
Erythromelalgia: avoid heat triggers, cooling (not ice), screen for myeloproliferative disease (JAK2)

pharmacological.regimen: Nifedipine 20-60 mg/day for persistent lesions; topical steroids for itch; treat underlying lupus if present
Aspirin for myeloproliferative-associated (dramatic response); neuropathic agents (gabapentinoids, SNRIs), mexiletine for erythermalgia; treat MPN (hydroxyurea)
Investigate APS, cholesterol emboli, vasculitis if persistent/irregular (livedo racemosa); keep warm; treat cause

diseases.disease: Atherosclerotic risk reduction / secondary prevention coordination
non_pharmacological: All patients with established ASCVD (coronary, cerebrovascular, PAD, AAA): smoking cessation, Mediterranean diet, exercise 150 min/week, weight management
Structured secondary prevention clinics improve outcomes; influenza vaccination

pharmacological.regimen: High-intensity statin (+ ezetimibe/PCSK9i/inclisiran per LDL targets); antiplatelet (aspirin or clopidogrel; DAPT short-term post-ACS/stent); ACEi/ARB; SGLT2i/GLP-1 RA in diabetes; rivaroxaban 2.5 mg BID + aspirin for high-risk stable PAD/CAD (COMPASS/VOYAGER)
Very high risk <1.4 mmol/L (55 mg/dL) and >=50% reduction; consider <1.0 mmol/L in recurrent events (ESC)

diseases.key_guideline: ESC 2024 CVD prevention; ACC/AHA secondary prevention
